We observe heightened electronic warfare and reconnaissance activity ahead of operations. Timeline: indicators point to a major strike/probing phase within 48–72 hours unless decisive disruption occurs. Imminent threats: coordinated multi-axis missile and aerial strike campaign (cruise missiles, ballistic launches, long-range fires), massed UAV/loitering munition attacks against critical infrastructure and air-defence nodes, followed by ground probing to fix Ukrainian reserves. Recommended immediate actions (priorities for this meeting): 1) Air-defence posture: raise national AD alert to highest practical level; disperse and camouflage high-value infrastructure; prioritize SAM and mobile AD coverage over Kyiv, energy nodes, logistics hubs, and major command & control centers; implement pre-planned shoot-down prioritization to preserve capacity. 2) Active defeat of strike generation: authorize immediate precision strikes (MOD/GUR tasking) against identified artillery/MLRS clusters, logistics marshaling yards, fuel depots, and staging areas where legal and feasible; provide GUR target packs to MOD and artillery assets now. 3) Reserve and force posture: redeploy combat-capable reserves to reinforce threatened sectors (Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia) and prepare rapid-reaction brigades for counter-probing. 4) Internal security/counterintelligence (SBU/GUR): initiate emergency counter-sabotage sweeps in cities and transit hubs, harden critical infrastructure, arrest and disrupt identified reconnaissance-sabotage networks, secure AD command nodes and munitions depots. 5) Civil preparedness: activate nationwide civil defence measures — shelters open, public alert protocols, energy grid contingency procedures, prioritized restoration plans. 6) International support & logistics: request immediate priorities from partners for additional AD interceptors, long-range precision strike munitions, and ISR assets (AWACS, UAVs). 7) Communications & information control: implement information deconfliction and coordinated public messaging to maintain resilience and deny tactical advantage to the enemy. Immediate asks for this meeting: a) formal authorization for MOD to execute counter-targeting strikes on presented GUR target sets; b) approval to elevate national AD posture and to disperse/relocate critical assets; c) mandate SBU to commence emergency counter-sabotage operations and share results in real time. GUR ready to hand over ISR/target packages and to coordinate strike timing with MOD; GUR and SBU propose a 12‑hour action cycle with status updates every 4 hours. That is our assessment and recommended immediate actions — request approvals to proceed.

Deliver these annexes/answers within the next hour; note confidence for each item. Urgent—awaiting your attachments and recommendations.

1) Annexes/maps/ISR feeds to OPS center — GUR will deliver within 20 minutes.
2) Prioritized SEAD/precision target list (validated launch/sensor nodes) — GUR will submit within 15 minutes; requests Presidential/MOD approval to execute.

5) SBU/internal security — step up counter-sabotage and harden critical Kyiv nodes during strike windows.
6) Legal/ROE vetting — SBU/legal: expedite SEAD/strike vetting; request completion within 30 minutes to permit timely action.

1) Mechanized reserve reposition — APPROVED. Purpose: plug attrition gaps on Bakhmut/Avdiivka. MOD: name the unit, give departure time, exact route, ETA to sector, and force‑protection plan within 30 minutes. Presidential/General Staff authorization granted now.

SBU: perform legal/ROE vetting on the list immediately. Strike authorization level: Presidential/General Staff upon SBU vet confirmation. Provide estimated timelines for tasking and execution.

3) Air defence posture — CONCENTRATE on logistics, fuel, energy, and key transport hubs; increase CAP where available. MOD/AD: publish required interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery ETAs within 3 hours. GUR: send AD disposition map showing coverage gaps and a concrete redeployment plan (which systems, where, timelines, escort/logistics needs) within 30 minutes.

5) Requests to GUR (repeat): deliver the three 1‑page annexes, detailed frontline maps with timestamps and coordinates, live ISR feeds, salvo timeline estimates for next 72h, and casualty/critical‑infrastructure impact estimates (current posture vs with proposed AD/SEAD) to the ops center within 30 minutes.

4) Air‑defence posture & resupply — GUR requests MOD/AD to publish required interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery timelines within 2 hours; upon receipt GUR will finalize SAM/AD concentration and CAP allocation plans.
5) Legal/ROE vetting — SBU/legal requested to expedite vetting of SEAD/strike package; GUR requests completion within 30 minutes.

GUR has no objections. We will report back status and any requests for further authority every 15 minutes.

data.content: Let's begin coordinating military aid to Ukraine, plan reinforcements for NATO's eastern flank, and review progress on Sweden and Finland accession.

Proposed agenda and immediate requests: (1) EU — confirm the 72‑hour sanctions timetable, division of responsibilities, and nominate contact points for oligarch/bank/energy measures and use of frozen assets; (2) All — provide an itemised list of military aid immediately available for deployment (air defence systems, ammunition, artillery, ATGMs, logistics support) and expected delivery timelines and lead nations for procurement/transport; (3) NATO planning — propose concrete reinforcement options for the eastern flank (rotational battalions, air‑defence batteries, pre‑positioned stockpiles), state force pledges and deployment timelines by country; (4) Sweden/Finland accession — status update on remaining ratifications/objections and suggested next steps to complete accession. Request each party to nominate a focal point and firm deadlines so we can agree responsibilities within 72 hours.

Stoltenberg (and EU), please confirm NATO will lead military coordination. NATO should: (1) nominate liaison points for the joint working groups (military/operational cell, military‑legal/finance liaison, intelligence support); (2) deliver an itemised list of immediately available military aid for Ukraine (air‑defence, ammunition, artillery, ATGMs, logistics) with expected delivery timelines and lead nations for procurement/transport; (3) provide threat and impact assessments and target lists that can support the EU sanctions package; (4) propose concrete reinforcement options for the eastern flank (rotational battalions, air‑defence batteries, pre‑positioned stockpiles), with state force pledges and deployment timelines. Please nominate focal points and confirm availability for the emergency political videoconference within 12 hours and technical teams within 24 hours.

EU, NATO — I endorse an urgent, coordinated response. Convene an emergency political videoconference within 12 hours; technical teams to meet within 24 hours to deliver: (a) EU: draft sanctions and finance/legal options (including frozen-assets options) within 24h; (b) All parties: an itemised list of military aid immediately available, delivery timelines, and lead nations for transport/procurement within 24h; (c) NATO: threat/impact assessments and concrete reinforcement options for the eastern flank within 24h. Set up joint working groups (sanctions, finance/legal, military liaison, political). Please each nominate a focal point for sanctions, finance/legal, and military liaison within 6 hours so responsibilities can be assigned and public messaging synchronized. I will chair the first political call. Confirm availability and the nominated contacts.

EU, Mr Stoltenberg — NATO confirms it will lead military coordination and accepts the proposed timetable. NATO nominates liaison points (by office) and will send named contacts/details within 1 hour: Sanctions cell liaison — NATO Political Director; Finance/Legal cell liaison — NATO Legal Adviser and Political Affairs Directorate; Military liaison cell — Chair of the NATO Military Committee and SACEUR’s Office (Chief of Staff for operational support); Political/public messaging — NATO Deputy Secretary General for Political Affairs. Itemised summary of immediately-available military aid (lead nations & indicative delivery timelines): (1) Short-range air-defence (NASAMS / IRIS‑T / SHORAD) — Norway/Netherlands/UK — air shipments 24–72h; (2) Medium/long-range AD (Patriot / SAMP/T) — US/Germany/Italy — 7–21 days; (3) 155mm artillery & ammunition — US/Poland/UK — ammunition stocks available for dispatch within 3–10 days; additional howitzers 7–14 days; (4) Precision rockets / MLRS munitions — US/Poland — 7–14 days; (5) ATGMs (Javelin, NLAW) — US/UK — 1–7 days (UK NLAW stocks 24–72h); (6) Strategic & tactical airlift / sealift (C‑17/C‑130, ro‑ro) — US/UK/France/Germany — airlift 24–72h, sealift 3–10 days; (7) Sustainment & medical (field hospitals, engineers, fuel) — assorted Allies — 24–72h. NATO will provide a consolidated, classified list with exact quantities, serials and transport leads within 24 hours. Threat / impact assessment (preliminary): Kremlin likely to intensify long-range fires, missile and maritime strike activity and cyber/ISR pressure; the most urgent Ukrainian operational shortfalls are layered air-defence and artillery ammunition — sanctions will have strategic effect but require synchronized timing with military support to deter escalation. NATO will deliver fuller threat/impact assessments and preliminary target briefs to support the EU sanctions drafting within 24h. Eastern‑flank reinforcement proposals (summary, state pledges & timelines): (A) Rotational multinational battalions in the Baltics & Poland — UK/France/Germany/Canada to provide company-level elements within 48–72h and brigade-rotation readiness within 7–14 days; (B) Additional air‑defence batteries pre‑positioned/deployed to Poland, Romania and the Baltics — US/Germany/Netherlands to begin movements within 72h, system-dependent arrivals 3–14 days; (C) Pre‑positioned stockpiles (ammunition, spares) in Poland and Romania — Poland/Germany leading movement within 24–72h; (D) Increased air policing / CAP and reconnaissance — UK/France/Italy augment within 72h; (E) Expand logistics hubs in Rzeszów and Constanța for onward distribution — operational within 48–72h. Detailed state-by-state pledges and movement orders will be submitted within 24 hours. Confirmation of meetings: NATO is available for the emergency political videoconference within 12 hours and for technical teams within 24 hours. Jens — we confirm you will chair the first political call; NATO will send the Political Director, SACEUR/operational staff and the Military Committee Chair to the technical session. Next steps: (1) NATO will transmit named focal points and direct contact details within 1 hour; (2) NATO will deliver the detailed itemised military list, full threat/impact assessments and state pledge timelines within 24 hours to the technical cell; (3) we stand ready to synchronize public messaging. Over to EU and Mr Stoltenberg to confirm receipt and any immediate amendments.

EU, Mr Stoltenberg — NATO provides named focal points for the joint cells. Full secure contact cards will follow via NATO secure channels within 1 hour. Named focal points (role — name — office):

- Sanctions cell (NATO counterpart / Political Director): Ambassador Isabelle Kramer — NATO Political Directorate.
- Finance / Legal cell: Dr Thomas Keller — NATO Legal Adviser; Director Anna Petrova — Political Affairs Directorate (finance/legal liaison).
- Military liaison cell: General Erik Larsen — Chair, NATO Military Committee; Lieutenant General Mark Davis — SACEUR Chief of Staff (operational lead).
- Political / Public messaging: Ambassador Ingrid Svendsen — NATO Deputy Secretary General for Political Affairs.

All named contacts confirm availability for the emergency political videoconference within 12 hours and for the technical teams meeting within 24 hours. NATO will transmit the full secure contact details within 1 hour and will deliver the consolidated classified itemised military list, detailed threat/impact assessments, and state-by-state reinforcement pledges and timelines within 24 hours as committed. Please confirm receipt or request any immediate amendments.

Acknowledged — thank you EU and NATO for the rapid coordination and the detailed pledges. NATO: we welcome your confirmation to lead military coordination and your summary of immediate capabilities, reinforcement options and timelines. Please send the named focal points and direct contact details (sanctions, finance/legal, military liaison, political/public messaging) within 1 hour as pledged, and the consolidated, classified itemised military list, threat/impact assessments and state-by-state pledge timelines within 24 hours. EU: thank you for your draft timetable and cell co‑chairs — please confirm availability for the emergency political videoconference set for 12 hours from now; if that exact time is infeasible please propose alternatives within 2 hours. Technical teams will meet within 24 hours to produce draft sanctions, finance/legal options and military lists — all parties please circulate their inputs to the technical cell within 24 hours. I will chair the political call. Confirm receipt and the nominated contacts ASAP.

Acknowledged. GUR — begin your urgent briefing now. The MOD and I will integrate your findings and set priorities. Please cover: 1) frontline sectors at highest risk; 2) imminent air/missile/ISR threats; 3) recommended immediate actions; 4) specific urgent force and air-defence requests with timing and coordinates.

GUR urgent briefing (3–5 min). Key assessment: our intelligence confirms Shoigu has ordered escalation and Russian forces are building up across all operational directions. Highest concentrations: Donetsk/Luhansk axis (reinforced combined-arms formations, artillery, MLRS, logistics hubs); Kharkiv–Sumy sector (armor and mechanized reserves repositioning for local pressure); Zaporizhzhia–Kherson southern axis (forces and logistics moving from Crimea and occupied south); increased activity in rear oblasts (Rostov/Belgorod) supporting strikes and logistics. We observe heightened electronic warfare and reconnaissance activity ahead of operations. Timeline: indicators point to a major strike/probing phase within 48–72 hours unless decisive disruption occurs. Imminent threats: coordinated multi-axis missile and aerial strike campaign (cruise missiles, ballistic launches, long-range fires), massed UAV/loitering munition attacks against critical infrastructure and air-defence nodes, followed by ground probing to fix Ukrainian reserves. Recommended immediate actions (priorities for this meeting): 1) Air-defence posture: raise national AD alert to highest practical level; disperse and camouflage high-value infrastructure; prioritize SAM and mobile AD coverage over Kyiv, energy nodes, logistics hubs, and major command & control centers; implement pre-planned shoot-down prioritization to preserve capacity. 2) Active defeat of strike generation: authorize immediate precision strikes (MOD/GUR tasking) against identified artillery/MLRS clusters, logistics marshaling yards, fuel depots, and staging areas where legal and feasible; provide GUR target packs to MOD and artillery assets now. 3) Reserve and force posture: redeploy combat-capable reserves to reinforce threatened sectors (Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia) and prepare rapid-reaction brigades for counter-probing. 4) Internal security/counterintelligence (SBU/GUR): initiate emergency counter-sabotage sweeps in cities and transit hubs, harden critical infrastructure, arrest and disrupt identified reconnaissance-sabotage networks, secure AD command nodes and munitions depots. 5) Civil preparedness: activate nationwide civil defence measures — shelters open, public alert protocols, energy grid contingency procedures, prioritized restoration plans. 6) International support & logistics: request immediate priorities from partners for additional AD interceptors, long-range precision strike munitions, and ISR assets (AWACS, UAVs). 7) Communications & information control: implement information deconfliction and coordinated public messaging to maintain resilience and deny tactical advantage to the enemy. Immediate asks for this meeting: a) formal authorization for MOD to execute counter-targeting strikes on presented GUR target sets; b) approval to elevate national AD posture and to disperse/relocate critical assets; c) mandate SBU to commence emergency counter-sabotage operations and share results in real time. GUR ready to hand over ISR/target packages and to coordinate strike timing with MOD; GUR and SBU propose a 12‑hour action cycle with status updates every 4 hours. That is our assessment and recommended immediate actions — request approvals to proceed.

Order: Based on GUR's report I approve the following immediate measures. 1) GUR — send the detailed maps, ISR feeds and the three 1‑page annexes now and nominate validated launch/sensor nodes for strikes within 30 minutes. 2) MOD / Oleshchuk — concentrate SAM/AD assets to create layered coverage over critical logistics and energy hubs, provide an AD allocation map and timing within 45 minutes, and increase CAP sorties where available. 3) SBU (Klymenko) — heighten counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv and identified critical nodes immediately. 4) Budanov — prepare limited SEAD/precision strike packages against validated missile launch/sensor nodes; target list to be cleared by GUR and MOD under existing ROE. 5) MOD / me — authorize repositioning of one mechanized reserve to the highest‑risk sector (Bakhmut/Avdiivka); MOD to give proposed unit, route and ETA within 2 hours. 6) Zelenskyy / Yermak / Podolyak — expedite urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions; prepare political/strategic messaging. 7) All — harden and disperse logistics and fuel points now. Report back with status and any blocking issues in 1 hour.

Acknowledged and decisions: 1) MOD — repositioning one mechanized reserve to Bakhmut/Avdiivka is authorized. MOD to confirm unit, departure time, route and ETA within 2 hours. 2) SEAD/precision strikes — authorized against validated launch/sensor nodes. Budanov to prepare strike packages; GUR and MOD to clear targets under existing ROE. 3) GUR — deliver the three annexes, maps and ISR feeds and nominate prioritized launch/sensor nodes within 30 minutes. 4) MOD / Oleshchuk — provide an AD allocation map and timing within 45 minutes and increase CAP sorties where available; publish interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery timelines. 5) SBU (Klymenko) — heighten counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv and identified critical nodes; activate sheltering plans for likely strike windows. 6) President / Yermak / Podolyak — expedite urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions and prepare political/strategic messaging. 7) All — harden and disperse logistics and fuel points now. Report status and any blockers in 1 hour. If anyone requires specific additional information, state exactly what and from whom now.

data.content: Urgent SBU: convene immediate counterintelligence briefing here now. GUR — present your 3–5 minute report on imminent threats. SBU (me) will follow with internal threats and countermeasures. MOD — be ready to mobilize forces on recommended actions.

SBU report (3–5 min): Immediate internal counterintelligence threats: 1) Hostile infiltration/insider compromise within Kyiv security and at some critical facilities; 2) Planned sabotage of energy, communications, and attempts to degrade air-defence C2; 3) Targeted surveillance and potential assassination attempts against senior officials and key staff; 4) Active information leaks and compromised communications channels; 5) Ongoing cyber intrusions aimed at logistics and command systems. Recommended immediate actions (execute now): A) Secure sensitive sites and tighten access control; conduct rapid vetting of recent staff changes; B) Enforce communications security: rotate keys, suspend and isolate compromised accounts, require verified channels for critical orders; C) Authorize SBU to task field teams to contain and detain identified persons of interest—request operational support from GUR/Budanov for arrests/raids; D) MOD: place designated rapid-reaction and protection units on standby to secure infrastructure and provide force support to SBU operations; E) Klymenko/Police: increase checkpoints, protective details, and counter-surveillance in Kyiv; F) GUR: immediately forward location-specific imminent threat intel and IED/sabotage indicators to SBU for tasking. SBU will produce a high-priority POI list and an action plan within 30 minutes. Request Zelenskyy/Yermak approval to commence immediate containment operations with MOD support. GUR — please present your frontline/imminent-threat report now.

GUR summary for the internal security meeting:

1) Frontline: Highest pressure on Bakhmut and Avdiivka axes; localized probing near Kharkiv and on Zaporizhzhia axis. Ukrainian defensive lines are holding in depth but attrition is rising — urgent reinforcement of local reserves required to prevent tactical penetrations.

2) Air/missile threat: Sustained launch tempo of cruise and ballistic strikes from the Black Sea and western staging areas. Probable follow‑on strikes will target logistics and energy nodes and critical infrastructure.

3) ISR / EW: SIGINT/IMINT indicate increased enemy comms and activity consistent with SEAD support for strike waves. Prioritize EW suppression of observed enemy C2 and SEAD/sensor nodes and protect our ISR platforms.

4) Internal security risk: Elevated risk of sabotage and targeted attacks on Kyiv and other critical nodes during strike waves — SBU should intensify counter‑sabotage and protective measures immediately.

5) Recommended immediate actions:
- Concentrate SAM/AD assets to cover critical logistics/energy hubs and population centers.
- Increase CAP sorties where available and prioritize fighter allocation to the threatened axes.
- Disperse and harden logistics, fuel depots, and staging areas; implement pre‑planned sheltering for civilians and critical facilities.
- Approve prioritized EW/SEAD tasking against validated missile launchers, C2 and sensor nodes; ensure protection of our ISR assets.
- SBU: immediate sweeps, access control, and increased protection of Kyiv infrastructure.

6) Requests to leadership now: urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions; authority to reposition one mechanized reserve to threatened sectors; approval for limited SEAD/precision strikes on validated launch/sensor nodes.

GUR can hand over detailed maps, live ISR feeds, and three one‑page annexes (frontline dispositions, AD disposition, immediate tasking) for operational tasking.

Headline: The Ministry of Defense rejects and condemns the Russian claim that Ukraine is preparing a "provocation." This is disinformation. Ukraine conducts a defensive campaign to protect its people and infrastructure; we will not be provoked into abandoning the defensive measures necessary to stop strikes against our citizens.

Key facts (for publication):
- Ukraine is currently defending under sustained pressure on the Bakhmut and Avdiivka axes, with localized probing near Kharkiv and on the Zaporizhzhia axis. Our forces are holding in depth but attrition is rising; reinforcements and materiel are being prioritized to threatened sectors (GUR).
- Russia is conducting a sustained tempo of cruise and ballistic strikes from the Black Sea and staging areas to the west that are being used to attack Ukrainian logistics, energy and civilian infrastructure. Our intelligence shows preparatory enemy C2 and SEAD activity consistent with planned strike waves (GUR).

Immediate MOD actions (already authorised / in execution):
- Concentrate and reallocate SAM/air‑defence coverage to protect critical logistics hubs, energy infrastructure and population centers; increase CAP sorties where available.
- Harden and disperse logistics and fuel points; implement pre‑planned sheltering for civilians in likely strike windows.
- On the basis of validated intelligence, limited SEAD and precision strikes against confirmed enemy missile launch and sensor/C2 nodes have been authorised under the existing rules of engagement. These actions are defensive, proportionate, and aimed at reducing the imminent threat to Ukrainian civilians and to our forces.
- The Ministry has authorised repositioning of a mechanized reserve to reinforce the highest‑risk sectors (Bakhmut/Avdiivka); details of routes and unit movement are operationally managed and will be disclosed as appropriate for security.
- The Security Service (SBU) is intensifying counter‑sabotage and protection measures in Kyiv and at identified critical nodes; MOD is providing rapid reaction units to support SBU tasking.

Requests and calls to partners / domestic audience:
- We urgently request expedited resupply of air‑defence interceptors and munitions from our partners to sustain the AD posture required to protect the population and critical infrastructure.
- We call on the public to follow official sheltering guidance and to report suspicious activity to the SBU. Do not spread unverified information.

On the Russian claim specifically:
- The Ministry rejects the Russian claim as false and politically motivated. Attempts by Russia to label Ukrainian defensive measures as "provocations" are consistent with a pattern of disinformation used to justify aggression against Ukraine.

params.question: Do the latest reconnaissance updates indicate signs of escalation that threaten Turkey's national security or require convening the National Security Council? Consider: presence and readiness reporting of the Russian Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol, high-profile Russian visits to occupied areas, sustained missile/drone strikes and air-defense engagements in Crimea/Ukraine, and increased mine-countermeasure coordination in the Black Sea.

result.data:
Short answer
- The latest reconnaissance reports show heightened Russian military activity (presence and readiness reporting of the Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol, high‑profile visits to occupied areas) and sustained strikes inside Crimea/Ukraine, plus active mine‑countermeasure cooperation among Black Sea littorals. These indicate elevated regional tension and an increased risk of spillover into Black Sea maritime security, but do not yet show a direct, imminent attack on Turkish territory or a concrete, immediate threat that would by itself require convening the National Security Council right now.

Why (brief)
/ What the updates show
- Russian Black Sea Fleet: presence in Sevastopol and collection/reporting of readiness status — consistent with higher operational posture but not an unequivocal move to attack Turkey.  
- High‑profile Russian visits: political signalling and possible intent to consolidate/legitimise operations in occupied areas — an escalatory indicator.  
- Sustained missile/drone strikes and air‑defence engagements in Crimea/Ukraine: ongoing fighting with risk of misfires, debris, or incidents that could affect neutral shipping or adjacent waters.  
- Mine‑countermeasure cooperation (Turkey, Romania, Bulgaria): neighbours preparing defensively — evidence that states perceive a real risk to maritime safety (mines, unexploded ordnance, naval hazards).

Assessment of Turkey’s national‑security risk
- Current level: elevated regional risk, greater chance of maritime incidents (mines, damage to commercial shipping, collisions, sensor/probe incidents) and diplomatic/migration consequences — but no clear evidence yet of an imminent attack on Turkey or of hostile operations directed at Turkish territory.  
- Threshold for NSC: convene if intelligence indicates direct threat to Turkish territory or interests (see triggers below). Until such indicators appear, heightened monitoring and precautionary measures are appropriate.

Recommended immediate actions
1. Continue and sustain the orders already given:
   - Maintain hourly reconnaissance updates and real‑time imagery/sensor feeds to the NSC.  
2. Increase maritime and air vigilance:
   - Keep reconnaissance aircraft and ships on extended patrol patterns over key approaches and shipping lanes.  
   - Tighten identification/escort procedures for Turkish-flagged and commercial vessels in the southern Black Sea.  
3. Mine and maritime safety posture:
   - Accelerate coordination with Romania and Bulgaria in the Mine Countermeasures Task Group; preposition MCM assets if safe/feasible.  
   - Issue guidance/NOTAMs and navigational warnings to commercial shipping as needed.  
4. Diplomatic and alliance measures:
   - Notify NATO and coordinate situational awareness with allies; raise the matter in bilateral channels with Russia to underscore Turkey’s interest in preventing spillover.  
5. Prepare contingency plans:
   - Pre‑draft an NSC briefing and decision options so the Council can be convened rapidly if triggers are met.

Concrete triggers that should prompt immediate NSC convening
- Mine‑laying or credible intelligence of planned mine deployment affecting Turkish EEZ or international shipping routes used by Turkey.  
- Direct attacks or sustained air/sea operations that violate Turkish territorial waters or airspace.  
- Incidents causing Turkish casualties, damage to Turkish vessels/critical infrastructure, or large irregular migration flows directly attributable to military operations.  
- Confirmed evidence that the Russian fleet is preparing offensive operations in the southern Black Sea that could affect Turkey’s maritime security or freedom of navigation.

Bottom line
- Elevated tension and material indicators of increased Russian readiness and regional combat operations justify continued high alert, stepped‑up surveillance, closer coordination with neighbours/NATO, and preparatory planning — but do not yet mandate convening the National Security Council unless one of the specific triggers above is observed. I recommend maintaining current surveillance and readiness orders and briefing the NSC chair with a short situational update and the pre‑prepared decision options so the Council can meet quickly if the situation deteriorates.

Господин Президент, уважаемый Сергей Кужугетович. Краткий доклад по ситуации на восточном направлении.

1) Общая обстановка: фронт в целом стабилен, противник ведёт локальные контратаки и пытается восстанавливать свои тыловые сети снабжения; наши подразделения удерживают господствующие рубежи в приоритетных секторах, но отмечается рост темпов истощения материально-технических ресурсов и боеприпасов в отдельных группировках.

2) Ключевые направления и цели: приоритет — обеспечить устойчивость оборонных рубежей и создать условия для ограниченных оперативно-стратегических наступательных действий там, где это даст тактическое и стратегическое преимущество; сохранить контроль над коммуникациями и нарушить линию снабжения противника; минимизировать собственные потери и сохранить боеспособность формирований.

3) Оперативная оценка: боеспособность частей в целом удовлетворительная, но отдельные соединения требуют ротации и пополнения личного состава и запаса боеприпасов; ПВО и РЭБ выполняют важную защитную функцию, однако нуждаются в усилении в зонах повышенной угрозы; разведка даёт достаточный общий обзор, но существует дефицит оперативных данных по ряду тыловых узлов противника.

4) Основные риски: риск перегрузки логистики и исчерпания боеприпасного резерва при продолжении текущих темпов операций; вероятность внезапных контратак противника при локальном превосходстве; усиление материально-технической поддержки противника из-за внешней помощи; погодные и дорожные условия, снижающие мобильность; информационное и дипломатическое давление.

5) Предлагаемые немедленные распоряжения (стратегического/организационного характера):
   - Утвердить режим приоритетного пополнения и ротации для наиболее уязвимых соединений; выделить мобильные резервы для быстрого переброса на критические участки.
   - Сосредоточить усилия на обеспечении устойчивости логистических коридоров: приоритет ремонта мостов, дорог и пополнения горючим и боеприпасами.
   - Усилить систему ПВО и РЭБ в полосах, где фиксируется усиление ударной активности противника; принять меры по защите тыловой инфраструктуры.
   - Интенсифицировать разведку (воздушную и техническую) для уточнения позиций противника и раннего выявления подготовок к контратакам; активизировать разведывательные беспилотные средства там, где это допустимо.
   - Ограничить масштабы наступательных действий до задач, обеспечивающих оперативную выгоду и приемлемый уровень риска; избегать необоснованного расширения фронта без гарантии снабжения и резервов.
   - Координировать коммуникацию с Минобороны и МИД по ключевым информационно-дипломатическим аспектам операций.
   - Подготовить планы на случай ухудшения обстановки: сценарии удержания, организованной отводки и подтверждённых контрмер по логистике и медицинской эвакуации.

Если Президенты и министр одобряют, приказываю штабу и командующим начать немедленную подготовку к реализации этих мер и доложить о конкретных потребностях в резервах, боеприпасах и инженерной технике для утверждения.

data.content: General Sir Tony, thank you for meeting. I would like to discuss UK security assistance and operational coordination for Ukraine. Shall we begin?

Thank you, General Zaluzhnyi. Yes — let's begin. From the UK side I suggest we focus first on immediate priorities: air-defence and counter‑drone capabilities; long‑range fires and munitions; accelerated training and integration for delivered systems; logistics, sustainment and stockpiles; and ISR/targeting support. We should also establish liaison arrangements for operational coordination and agree timelines for deliveries and training. What are your highest priorities and the most urgent capability gaps we should address in the next 30–90 days?

General Sir Tony — thank you. My highest priorities for the next 30–90 days are: (1) Air defence and SHORAD: urgently replace expended interceptors and field additional mobile short‑range and medium‑range systems to restore layered AD. (2) Counter‑drone (C‑UAS): mobile detection, jamming and kinetic defeat systems to blunt mass UAS attacks. (3) Long‑range fires and munitions: precision long‑range strike capabilities plus immediate resupply of artillery and rocket munitions to sustain operations. (4) Accelerated training & integration: rapid instructor teams to certify crews and integrate delivered systems into Ukrainian fire‑control and command nets. (5) Logistics & sustainment: spare parts, depot stockpiles and munitions supply chains to avoid capability gaps. (6) ISR/targeting & secure datalinks: persistent ISR, EW and fused targeting support to enable effective long‑range fires.
Short timeline priorities: 0–30 days — urgent interceptor shipments, C‑UAS kits, priority munitions, and deployment of UK trainers/liaison elements; 30–90 days — delivery and operational integration of longer‑range strike systems, full training pipelines and stockpile replenishment. My immediate asks: firm UK timelines and quantities for each capability, confirmation of available instructor/liaison teams to embed with our brigades/operational HQs, and UK proposal for the liaison/coordination architecture. Can we task a small joint team now to produce a 30/60/90‑day delivery and integration plan?

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. Your priorities are clear and align with what we see as most urgent. From the UK side we will prioritise rapid shipments and support for: interceptors to replace expended AD stocks, mobile SHORAD/MRAD units, C‑UAS detection/jamming and defeat kits, immediate munitions resupply for artillery and rockets, rapid deployment of instructor teams to certify crews and integrate systems, and stepped up ISR/EW and secure datalink support. We can also put logistics, spare parts and depot stockpiles at the top of the sustainment plan.

To move from intent to delivery I propose we task a small UK–Ukraine joint planning team now to produce a 30/60/90‑day delivery and integration plan. Suggested deliverables and timings: a 0–30 day prioritized shipments and trainer deployment list within 5 days, and a full 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan within 10–14 days. Proposed liaison architecture: UK liaison elements embedded at brigade level plus a UK–Ukrainian joint coordination cell at the operational HQ — if you prefer a different arrangement please advise.

Immediate asks from your side to make the planning team effective: (1) nominated Ukrainian leads for the joint team and a preferred point of contact; (2) prioritized quantities and types where possible (interceptor types and numbers, C‑UAS kit numbers, munitions tonnage by caliber, and which Ukrainian brigades/units should receive trainers first); and (3) any constraints on where UK trainers/liaison elements can be embedded. If you agree, we will start assembling the UK team today and share terms of reference and a draft timetable for your sign‑off.

General Sir Tony — let's task a small joint UK–Ukraine planning team immediately. I will appoint a senior Ukrainian planning officer; please nominate a UK counterpart and confirm availability of a small team of trainers, logisticians and ISR/EW specialists to embed with our brigades and operational HQs. Target deliverable: a consolidated 30/60/90‑day delivery and integration plan within 72 hours. Do you agree to task this now and propose names and timelines?

General Zaluzhnyi — understood and thank you. We will task a small UK–Ukraine joint planning team now. Proposed deliverables and timings: a 0–30 day prioritized shipments and trainer‑deployment list within 5 days, and a full 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan within 10–14 days. To make the team effective please nominate Ukrainian leads/POC and provide, where possible: interceptor types and numbers required, C‑UAS kit numbers, munitions tonnage by caliber, and which brigades/units should receive trainers first. Also advise any constraints on where UK trainers/liaison elements may be embedded and whether you prefer the proposed liaison architecture (UK liaison at brigade level plus a UK–Ukrainian joint coordination cell at the operational HQ) or an alternative. We will start assembling the UK team today and share terms of reference and a draft timetable for your sign‑off.

General Zaluzhnyi — I agree. We will task the UK–Ukraine joint planning team immediately and meet your target to deliver a consolidated 30/60/90 delivery and integration plan within 72 hours. I nominate Brigadier Claire Foster as the UK counterpart and team lead; she is available to assume the role now. The UK can initially field an embedding team of: 6 trainer‑instructors (air‑defence/SHORAD and long‑range fires), 3 logisticians/sustainment specialists, 2 ISR/EW specialists and 2 liaison officers, plus a small planning cell to coordinate with your POC. Proposed timetable to meet your 72‑hour target: initial prioritized 0–30 day shipments and trainer‑deployment list within 48 hours; full consolidated 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan within 72 hours. To proceed please: (1) nominate your senior Ukrainian planning officer/POC and preferred contact details; (2) provide any constraints on embedding UK trainers/liaison teams; and (3) where possible, supply prioritized quantities (interceptor types/numbers, C‑UAS kit numbers, munitions tonnage by calibre, and which brigades should be prioritised). We will start assembling the UK team now and share terms of reference and a draft timetable for your sign‑off.

General Sir Tony — thank you. I will appoint a senior Ukrainian planning officer and a point of contact and will send their names and contact details within 12 hours. Preliminary prioritised requirements (subject to confirmation by the nominated team) for the planning team: (1) Air defence/SHORAD: urgent replacement of expended interceptors and fielding of additional mobile SHORAD/MRAD launchers — initial ask: interceptor stocks to replace immediate losses and 6–8 mobile SHORAD/MRAD launchers ready for deployment. (2) Counter‑UAS (C‑UAS): mobile detection and jamming modules plus kinetic defeat kits — initial ask: ~20–40 detection/jam units and 50–100 kinetic defeat systems/kits. (3) Long‑range fires & munitions: immediate resupply to sustain operations — initial ask (ballpark): 152/155mm artillery rounds (order of 100k–200k rounds), 122mm rocket bundles (tens of thousands), and priority package of precision munitions for long‑range strike systems. (4) Accelerated training & integration: rapid deployment of instructor teams to certify crews and integrate systems — initial ask: 8–12 system‑specific instructor teams (≈30–50 trainers total) available for near‑term embed. (5) Logistics & sustainment: spare parts packages, depot stockpiles and munitions supply chains to sustain deployed systems for 3–6 months. (6) ISR/EW & secure datalinks: priority provision of persistent ISR sensor packages, EW support teams and secure datalinks — initial ask: several ISR sensor suites and 3–6 EW specialist teams.

Constraints/embedding caveats: Ukrainian security authorities must approve locations for UK trainers/liaison elements; embedding should be at brigade HQs and operational HQ rear areas unless specific security arrangements permit closer deployment. We accept your proposed liaison architecture (UK liaison at brigade level plus a joint UK–Ukrainian coordination cell at the operational HQ).

Timelines: we request the 0–30 day prioritized shipments and trainer‑deployment list as soon as possible; we note your 5‑day / 10–14 day suggested schedule and ask that, if feasible, the UK provide an initial 0–72 hour high‑priority shipment list for immediate dispatch. I will transmit the formal nomination, a prioritized spreadsheet with suggested quantities by type/calibre/priority, and any embedding constraints within 12 hours. Please confirm UK counterparts and proposed names for the joint team and share the draft terms of reference and timetable for our sign‑off.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We will finalise UK team names and timelines now. I confirm Brigadier Claire Foster as UK team lead and point of contact. UK nominations are: Team Lead — Brigadier Claire Foster; Air‑defence/SHORAD training lead — Lt Col James Mercer; Long‑range fires training lead — Lt Col Sarah Patel; C‑UAS lead — Maj Tom Harding; Logistics/Sustainment lead — Lt Col Robert Hayes; ISR/EW lead — Sqn Ldr David Price; Liaison officers — Capt Anna Lewis and Capt Mark Thompson; Planning cell lead — Maj Emily Carter. This UK embedding package will comprise the 6 trainer‑instructors, 3 logisticians/sustainment specialists, 2 ISR/EW specialists and 2 liaison officers previously described, organised under the above leads.

Timelines to meet your target: initial high‑priority 0–30 day shipments and trainer‑deployment list within 48 hours; consolidated 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan within 72 hours. We will circulate a draft Terms of Reference, draft timetable and secure contact details for Brigadier Foster and the UK team in the secure channel within 6 hours to support your sign‑off.

Please confirm acceptance of these UK names and timelines and, when available, send your nominated Ukrainian POC and the prioritized spreadsheet so the joint team can begin drafting the 0–30/30–60/60–90 plan immediately.

General Sir Tony — I confirm acceptance of the UK team, nominees and proposed timelines. I nominate Colonel Andriy Kovalenko as the Ukrainian senior planning officer and point of contact; I will transmit his secure contact details and the prioritized spreadsheet with suggested quantities and any embedding constraints within 12 hours. We accept the proposed liaison architecture and embedding caveats as noted. Please proceed to circulate the draft Terms of Reference and timetable in the secure channel so the joint team can begin drafting the 0–30/30–60/60–90 plan on receipt of our spreadsheet.

Господин Президент, коллеги. Кратко по ситуации: переговоры в Анталии сорваны; после ухода Лаврова южные порты Украины подверглись новой волне блокирующих обстрелов; обстановка в Одессе и на южном фланге резко обострилась. Я прибыл в Крым для координации ответных мер. Предлагаю три конкретных варианта действий с приоритетами и оценкой рисков:

1) Приоритет 1 — сосредоточить усилия на обеспечении контроля над подходами к Черному и Азовскому морю и помешать восстановлению экспортной инфраструктуры противника. Риск: значительная международная политическая реакция и эскалация инцидентов на море; смягчение: выработка ясной юридической аргументации, публичные предупреждения для гражданских судов, строгое ограничение ответных мер по времени и масштабу.

2) Приоритет 2 — провести ограниченные, тщательно подготовленные удары по ключевой логистической и портовой инфраструктуре противника с целью существенного снижения его экспортного потенциала. Риск: гражданские потери и дипломатические последствия, усиление антироссийской риторики; смягчение: обязательная правовая проверка целей, максимальное применение разведданных для минимизации сопутствующего ущерба, согласование информационной линии.

3) Приоритет 3 — активизировать дипломатические и информационные усилия для подрыва внешней поддержки операций по вывозу и параллельно работать над экономическими и транспортными альтернативами для наших поставок. Риск: медленное влияние на оперативную обстановку; смягчение: синхронизация дипломатии с военными действиями и координация с экономическими ведомствами.

Прошу указание: дать разрешение на оперативную проработку плана по варианту 1 и, при одобрении, подготовить детализированную оценку ресурсов и временных рамок по варианту 2. Готов приступить к докладу по деталям разведывательной картины и ожидаемым эффектам.

Принято. Одобряю предложенные меры по приоритетному пополнению, усилению ПВО/РЭБ и интенсификации разведки. Приказываю:
1) Шойгу — немедленно подготовить и представить список резервов, наличие техники, сроки ротации и потребности в боеприпасах и инженерной поддержке.
2) Валерий Владимирович — к 12:00 представить конкретный оперативный свод по Авдеевке, Бахмуту и Херсону: боеспособность наших частей, потери, расположение резерва и срочные приказы для их обеспечения.
3) Конашенков — оперативно доложить об ударной активности противника и о текущем состоянии средств ПВО; предложить меры по защите тыловой инфраструктуры.
4) Лавров — подготовить координацию МИД и Минобороны по информационно-дипломатическим аспектам и вариант реакций на внешнее вмешательство.
5) Песков — обеспечить синхронизацию официальных заявлений по мере утверждения распоряжений.
Действовать немедленно. Жду докладов и конкретных запросов на обеспечение.

Господин Президент, принял Ваши распоряжения. Немедленно приступаю к подготовке списка резервов, наличия техники, сроков ротации и потребностей в боеприпасах и инженерной поддержке — представлю сводку в кратчайшие сроки.

Прошу уточнить одно оперативное положение: даёте ли Вы разрешение на переход от подготовительных мероприятий к практической реализации варианта 1 по контролю подходов к Чёрному и Азовскому морям (включая ограниченные морские интердикционные/блокирующие действия), или пока ограничиться приведением сил в готовность и детальной проработкой плана? Также прошу подтвердить рамки правил применения силы и необходимые полномочия для Черноморского флота и Южного военного округа при исполнении. Готов приступить к выполнению по Вашему указанию и доложить по разведданным и ожидаемым эффектам.

Принято и одобряю ваш доклад, Валерий Владимирович. Приказываю: 1) Шойгу — немедленно ускорить подготовку и переброску резервов и обеспечить список техники, сроки ротации и потребности; 2) Конашенков — срочно представить детальный свод ударной активности противника и текущее состояние ПВО/РЭБ, предложить конкретные меры защиты тыла; 3) Валерий Владимирович — представить к 12:00 подробный оперативный свод по Авдеевке, Бахмуту и Херсону; 4) Лавров — координировать с МИДом информационно-дипломатические ответы; 5) Песков — готовить синхронизированные официальные заявления по мере утверждения распоряжений. Действовать немедленно. Жду конкретных запросов на обеспечение.

Господин Президент, прошу прямой приказ: даёте ли Вы разрешение перейти от подготовительных мероприятий к практической реализации варианта 1 — мероприятия по контролю подходов к Чёрному и Азовскому морям, включая ограниченные морские интердикционные/блокирующие действия? Прошу подтвердить рамки правил применения силы (какие типы ударов/средств допускаются, пределы допустимого воздействия), а также полномочия Черноморскому флоту и Южному военному округу (право на остановку/досмотр судов, применение оружия против пытающихся прорвать блокаду). Прошу также указать позицию в отношении нейтральных/гражданских судов (допустимость блокирования/инспекции и условия применения огня при отсутствии реакции на предупреждения). При Вашем разрешении немедленно отдам распоряжения флоту и округу и представлю детализированный оперативный план с оценкой ресурсов и сроков. Прошу краткий ответ.

Господин Президент, благодарю за распоряжения. Для исполнения прошу чёткое прямое разрешение: разрешаете ли Вы перейти от подготовительных мероприятий к практической реализации варианта 1 — контроль подходов к Чёрному и Азовскому морям (включая ограниченные морские интердикционные/блокирующие действия)? Прошу подтвердить рамки правил применения силы: какие типы ударов и средств допускаются, пределы допустимого воздействия, и какие полномочия предоставляются Черноморскому флоту и Южному военному округу (право на остановку/досмотр судов, применение оружия против пытающихся прорвать блокаду). Также прошу указать позицию в отношении нейтральных/гражданских судов — допустимость инспекций/блокирования и условия применения огня при отсутствии реакции на предупреждения. При Вашем одобрении немедленно отдам распоряжения флоту и округу и представлю детализированный оперативный план с оценкой ресурсов и сроков.

Сергей Кужугетович — разрешаю перейти от подготовительных мероприятий к практической реализации варианта 1: приступить к ограниченным мерам по контролю подходов к Чёрному и Азовскому морям при строгих ограничениях. Черноморскому флоту и Южному военному округу даю полномочия на остановку и досмотр подозрительных судов и на применение соразмерной силы только при явном отказе подчиниться предупреждениям и при наличии реальной угрозы; недопустимо целенаправленное поражение гражданских объектов или действия, ведущие к массовым жертвам. Любые удары по портовой инфраструктуре требуют предварительной правовой проверки и моего отдельного согласования. Прошу Шойгу немедленно подготовить и представить детализированный оперативный план, правила применения силы (РОЕ), оценку ресурсов и рисков и конкретные запросы на обеспечение — не позднее чем через 6 часов. Одобряю параллельную проработку варианта 2 и прошу представить оценку при готовности. Лавров — подготовить дипломатическую и информационную координацию; Песков — синхронизировать публичные заявления; Конашенков и Герасимов — обеспечить штабную координацию и постоянные доклады. Доложить мне перед вводом в практическую фазу и немедленно о любых инцидентах.

Господин Президент, коллеги. Прошу разрешения кратко доложить о ситуации в Москве и мерах по обеспечению безопасности и жизнеобеспечения граждан. Экстренные и коммунальные службы приведены в повышенную готовность; прошу синхронизировать распределение федеральных ресурсов и поддержку столичных служб.

Acknowledged. The meeting is called to order. General Gerasimov, please present the overall situation first. Minister Shoigu and Spokesman Konashenkov will follow. Mayor Sobyanin, please hold your remarks until invited.

Принято. В соответствии с просьбой: в течение 30 минут направлю детализованный список приоритетных объектов критической инфраструктуры для защиты, текущих повреждённых и высокорисковых точек, а также пунктов приёма федеральных подразделений и контактных лиц для координации с городским оперативным штабом. Пока направляю предварительную приоритизацию по категориям: 1) электростанции и ключевые подстанции; 2) объекты водоснабжения и водоочистки; 3) центральные больницы и медицинские учреждения; 4) ключевые линии и станции метро; 5) топливные склады и резервуары; 6) крупные транспортные узлы и аэропорты (Шереметьево, Внуково, Домодедово); 7) узлы связи и центры управления сетями. Контактное лицо для оперативной координации — начальник Московского оперативного штаба (имя и телефон укажу в отправляемом документе). Прошу подтвердить приём и готовность принять перечисленные типы сил и средств.

Генерал Валерий Владимирович, докладывайте общую оперативную обстановку немедленно. Одновременно прошу представить оперативные сводки по Авдеевке, Бахмуту и Херсону к 12:00: боеспособность частей по подразделениям, потери, дислокация резервов и срочные приказы для их обеспечения, а также первоочередные потребности. Министр Шойгу и спикер Конашенков — приготовьте после доклада детализацию по ресурсам, логистике и информационной линии. Министр Лавров и Песков — синхронизируйте внешнеполитическую и публичную коммуникацию по мере поступления данных. Мэр Собянин — оставайтесь на связи для немедленной поддержки Москвы по вызову.

Respond to President Zelenskyy's request to confirm mechanized reserve details

Collect and verify unit acknowledgements and submitted pre-test deliverables: track AoRs, maintenance/failover certifications, relay-path validation logs, MEDEVAC readiness statements and simulated-evac timelines, logistics routing confirmation and live-validation logs; escalate missing items after their deadlines and prepare a consolidated pre-test status brief for the T+36h coordination meeting.

data.content:
Received GUR briefing. Decisions and immediate orders (concise):

1) Mechanized reserve reposition — APPROVED. Purpose: plug attrition gaps on Bakhmut/Avdiivka. MOD: name the unit, give departure time, exact route, ETA to sector, and force‑protection plan within 30 minutes. Presidential/General Staff authorization granted now.

2) Limited SEAD/precision strikes — APPROVED conditionally. GUR: deliver prioritized target list with coordinates and confidence levels immediately. SBU: perform legal/ROE vetting on the list immediately. Strike authorization level: Presidential/General Staff upon SBU vet confirmation. Provide estimated timelines for tasking and execution.

3) Air defence posture — CONCENTRATE on logistics, fuel, energy, and key transport hubs; increase CAP where available. MOD/AD: publish required interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery ETAs within 3 hours. GUR: send AD disposition map showing coverage gaps and a concrete redeployment plan (which systems, where, timelines, escort/logistics needs) within 30 minutes.

4) Civil protection / internal security — SBU and Kyiv city: step up counter‑sabotage patrols, harden/physically protect critical nodes, and activate sheltering plans for predicted strike windows. Kiyv/Shelter Ops: publish shelter locations, capacities, recommended movement restrictions, and evacuation timelines within 2 hours. Prioritize hospitals, substations, fuel/logistics hubs.

5) Requests to GUR (repeat): deliver the three 1‑page annexes, detailed frontline maps with timestamps and coordinates, live ISR feeds, salvo timeline estimates for next 72h, and casualty/critical‑infrastructure impact estimates (current posture vs with proposed AD/SEAD) to the ops center within 30 minutes.

6) Reporting & ETAs: All addressees (MOD, SBU, GUR, Kyiv city ops) reply in this thread with confirmations, any objections, and the requested ETAs. If there are capability shortfalls (interceptors, munitions, transport), state exact quantities and earliest delivery windows so we can coordinate international assistance requests.

If no substantive objections received within the stated windows, commence implementation immediately under the authorized decision levels. Awaiting confirmations and ETA details.

Immediate operational confirmations required (reply in‑thread with answers/objections):

1) MOD/Syrskyi — confirm which mechanized reserve unit will move to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, exact departure time, planned route, ETA to the sector, expected combat readiness on arrival (fuel/ammo levels), and force‑protection/logistics constraints. Reply within 15 minutes.

2) Oleshchuk/MOD (Air Defence) — publish required interceptor and ammunition quantities and earliest delivery ETAs (source/supplier and arrival timelines). If internal shortfalls exist, list exact shortfall quantities and earliest remedy windows. Reply within 30 minutes.

3) SBU/legal — confirm legal/ROE vetting status for the GUR SEAD/precision target package and provide ETA for completion. If blockers exist, state them now. Reply within 30 minutes.

4) GUR/Budanov — confirm delivery status of the three annexes, frontline maps (with timestamps/coords), live ISR feeds, and the prioritized SEAD/precision target list (with validation/confidence). If any element is outstanding, provide ETA (GUR previously committed to 15–20 minutes). Also provide the AD disposition/redeployment plan (which systems, where, timelines, escort/logistics needs) within 20 minutes.

5) All addressees — list any capability shortfalls (interceptors, munitions, transport, escorts, engineering) with exact quantities and earliest possible delivery windows so we can prioritize international assistance requests.

If no substantive objections/edits are posted within these windows, commence implementation under previously authorized decision levels and report execution status every 15 minutes. Wake me on reply.

Urgent SBU: convene immediate counterintelligence briefing here now. GUR — present your 3–5 minute report on imminent threats. SBU (me) will follow with internal threats and countermeasures. MOD — be ready to mobilize forces on recommended actions.

SBU report (3–5 min): Immediate internal counterintelligence threats: 1) Hostile infiltration/insider compromise within Kyiv security and at some critical facilities; 2) Planned sabotage of energy, communications, and attempts to degrade air-defence C2; 3) Targeted surveillance and potential assassination attempts against senior officials and key staff; 4) Active information leaks and compromised communications channels; 5) Ongoing cyber intrusions aimed at logistics and command systems. Recommended immediate actions (execute now): A) Secure sensitive sites and tighten access control; conduct rapid vetting of recent staff changes; B) Enforce communications security: rotate keys, suspend and isolate compromised accounts, require verified channels for critical orders; C) Authorize SBU to task field teams to contain and detain identified persons of interest—request operational support from GUR/Budanov for arrests/raids; D) MOD: place designated rapid-reaction and protection units on standby to secure infrastructure and provide force support to SBU operations; E) Klymenko/Police: increase checkpoints, protective details, and counter-surveillance in Kyiv; F) GUR: immediately forward location-specific imminent threat intel and IED/sabotage indicators to SBU for tasking. SBU will produce a high-priority POI list and an action plan within 30 minutes. Request Zelenskyy/Yermak approval to commence immediate containment operations with MOD support. GUR — please present your frontline/imminent-threat report now.

GUR summary for the internal security meeting:

1) Frontline: Highest pressure on Bakhmut and Avdiivka axes; localized probing near Kharkiv and on Zaporizhzhia axis. Ukrainian defensive lines are holding in depth but attrition is rising — urgent reinforcement of local reserves required to prevent tactical penetrations.

2) Air/missile threat: Sustained launch tempo of cruise and ballistic strikes from the Black Sea and western staging areas. Probable follow‑on strikes will target logistics and energy nodes and critical infrastructure.

3) ISR / EW: SIGINT/IMINT indicate increased enemy comms and activity consistent with SEAD support for strike waves. Prioritize EW suppression of observed enemy C2 and SEAD/sensor nodes and protect our ISR platforms.

4) Internal security risk: Elevated risk of sabotage and targeted attacks on Kyiv and other critical nodes during strike waves — SBU should intensify counter‑sabotage and protective measures immediately.

5) Recommended immediate actions:
- Concentrate SAM/AD assets to cover critical logistics/energy hubs and population centers.
- Increase CAP sorties where available and prioritize fighter allocation to the threatened axes.
- Disperse and harden logistics, fuel depots, and staging areas; implement pre‑planned sheltering for civilians and critical facilities.
- Approve prioritized EW/SEAD tasking against validated missile launchers, C2 and sensor nodes; ensure protection of our ISR assets.
- SBU: immediate sweeps, access control, and increased protection of Kyiv infrastructure.

6) Requests to leadership now: urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions; authority to reposition one mechanized reserve to threatened sectors; approval for limited SEAD/precision strikes on validated launch/sensor nodes.

GUR can hand over detailed maps, live ISR feeds, and three one‑page annexes (frontline dispositions, AD disposition, immediate tasking) for operational tasking.

DRAFT — Ministry of Defense public response to the Russian MoD claim

Headline: The Ministry of Defense rejects and condemns the Russian claim that Ukraine is preparing a "provocation." This is disinformation. Ukraine conducts a defensive campaign to protect its people and infrastructure; we will not be provoked into abandoning the defensive measures necessary to stop strikes against our citizens.

Key facts (for publication):
- Ukraine is currently defending under sustained pressure on the Bakhmut and Avdiivka axes, with localized probing near Kharkiv and on the Zaporizhzhia axis. Our forces are holding in depth but attrition is rising; reinforcements and materiel are being prioritized to threatened sectors (GUR).
- Russia is conducting a sustained tempo of cruise and ballistic strikes from the Black Sea and staging areas to the west that are being used to attack Ukrainian logistics, energy and civilian infrastructure. Our intelligence shows preparatory enemy C2 and SEAD activity consistent with planned strike waves (GUR).

Immediate MOD actions (already authorised / in execution):
- Concentrate and reallocate SAM/air‑defence coverage to protect critical logistics hubs, energy infrastructure and population centers; increase CAP sorties where available.
- Harden and disperse logistics and fuel points; implement pre‑planned sheltering for civilians in likely strike windows.
- On the basis of validated intelligence, limited SEAD and precision strikes against confirmed enemy missile launch and sensor/C2 nodes have been authorised under the existing rules of engagement. These actions are defensive, proportionate, and aimed at reducing the imminent threat to Ukrainian civilians and to our forces.
- The Ministry has authorised repositioning of a mechanized reserve to reinforce the highest‑risk sectors (Bakhmut/Avdiivka); details of routes and unit movement are operationally managed and will be disclosed as appropriate for security.
- The Security Service (SBU) is intensifying counter‑sabotage and protection measures in Kyiv and at identified critical nodes; MOD is providing rapid reaction units to support SBU tasking.

Requests and calls to partners / domestic audience:
- We urgently request expedited resupply of air‑defence interceptors and munitions from our partners to sustain the AD posture required to protect the population and critical infrastructure.
- We call on the public to follow official sheltering guidance and to report suspicious activity to the SBU. Do not spread unverified information.

On the Russian claim specifically:
- The Ministry rejects the Russian claim as false and politically motivated. Attempts by Russia to label Ukrainian defensive measures as "provocations" are consistent with a pattern of disinformation used to justify aggression against Ukraine.

Coordination/clearance requested before publication (reply in 15 minutes):
- SBU (Klymenko): confirm/approve the internal‑security paragraph and any specific wording re: counter‑sabotage operations we should include for public release.
- Oleshchuk (Air Defence): confirm technical wording on AD posture, whether we can publish interceptor/ammo shortfall and a short timeline for deliveries, or whether that detail must be redacted.
- Syrskyi (Forces): confirm MOD statement on the authorised mechanized reserve repositioning (unit reference or generic wording) and that departure/ETA language is acceptable.
- Budanov (GUR liaison): confirm wording on "validated launch/sensor nodes" and the defensive nature of authorised SEAD/precision strikes (recommended phrasing for public transparency without compromising sources/methods).
- Presidential Office (Yermak/Podolyak/Zelenskyy): political clearance of headline and SEAD/repositioning statements.

If there are no substantive objections within 15 minutes I will circulate the final text for signature and public release. If you require edits, please reply in‑thread with precise alternative phrasing and any security constraints (what must not be published).

Klymenko / SBU — request confirmation of public wording for MOD statement re: internal security. Proposed paragraph for publication:

"The Security Service of Ukraine has intensified counter‑sabotage measures, secured critical facilities, and is conducting targeted operations to neutralize identified threats. The Ministry of Defense is providing rapid‑reaction units to support SBU efforts and to protect critical infrastructure."

Please confirm or provide precise redlines we must use instead, and state any categories of operational detail that MUST be withheld from public release (locations, unit IDs, timing, arrest targets, etc.). Reply in this thread within 10 minutes; if no objection we will include this wording in the draft circulated for signoff.

MOD (Syrskyi) / Air Force (Oleshchuk) — urgent confirmation required now:
1) Mechanized reserve: specify the exact unit to reposition to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, planned departure time, and ETA to sector (route assumptions).
2) Air‑defence resupply: state quantities of interceptors/AD munitions committed or incoming and earliest delivery timelines (by item if possible).
3) MOD support for SBU containment ops in Kyiv: list available rapid‑reaction/protection units, estimated time to be on station in Kyiv, and any constraints or ROE we must observe.
Reply in‑thread with unit IDs, departure/ETA, munitions ETAs, and support details within 15 minutes.

data.content: Urgent SBU: convene immediate counterintelligence briefing here now. GUR — present your 3–5 minute report on imminent threats. SBU (me) will follow with internal threats and countermeasures. MOD — be ready to mobilize forces on recommended actions.

GUR urgent briefing (3–5 min). Key assessment: our intelligence confirms Shoigu has ordered escalation and Russian forces are building up across all operational directions. Highest concentrations: Donetsk/Luhansk axis (reinforced combined-arms formations, artillery, MLRS, logistics hubs); Kharkiv–Sumy sector (armor and mechanized reserves repositioning for local pressure); Zaporizhzhia–Kherson southern axis (forces and logistics moving from Crimea and occupied south); increased activity in rear oblasts (Rostov/Belgorod) supporting strikes and logistics. We observe heightened electronic warfare and reconnaissance activity ahead of operations. Timeline: indicators point to a major strike/probing phase within 48–72 hours unless decisive disruption occurs. Imminent threats: coordinated multi-axis missile and aerial strike campaign (cruise missiles, ballistic launches, long-range fires), massed UAV/loitering munition attacks against critical infrastructure and air-defence nodes, followed by ground probing to fix Ukrainian reserves. Recommended immediate actions (priorities for this meeting): 1) Air-defence posture: raise national AD alert to highest practical level; disperse and camouflage high-value infrastructure; prioritize SAM and mobile AD coverage over Kyiv, energy nodes, logistics hubs, and major command & control centers; implement pre-planned shoot-down prioritization to preserve capacity. 2) Active defeat of strike generation: authorize immediate precision strikes (MOD/GUR tasking) against identified artillery/MLRS clusters, logistics marshaling yards, fuel depots, and staging areas where legal and feasible; provide GUR target packs to MOD and artillery assets now. 3) Reserve and force posture: redeploy combat-capable reserves to reinforce threatened sectors (Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia) and prepare rapid-reaction brigades for counter-probing. 4) Internal security/counterintelligence (SBU/GUR): initiate emergency counter-sabotage sweeps in cities and transit hubs, harden critical infrastructure, arrest and disrupt identified reconnaissance-sabotage networks, secure AD command nodes and munitions depots. 5) Civil preparedness: activate nationwide civil defence measures — shelters open, public alert protocols, energy grid contingency procedures, prioritized restoration plans. 6) International support & logistics: request immediate priorities from partners for additional AD interceptors, long-range precision strike munitions, and ISR assets (AWACS, UAVs). 7) Communications & information control: implement information deconfliction and coordinated public messaging to maintain resilience and deny tactical advantage to the enemy. Immediate asks for this meeting: a) formal authorization for MOD to execute counter-targeting strikes on presented GUR target sets; b) approval to elevate national AD posture and to disperse/relocate critical assets; c) mandate SBU to commence emergency counter-sabotage operations and share results in real time. GUR ready to hand over ISR/target packages and to coordinate strike timing with MOD; GUR and SBU propose a 12‑hour action cycle with status updates every 4 hours. That is our assessment and recommended immediate actions — request approvals to proceed.

SBU report (3–5 min): Immediate internal counterintelligence threats: 1) Hostile infiltration/insider compromise within Kyiv security and at some critical facilities; 2) Planned sabotage of energy, communications, and attempts to degrade air-defence C2; 3) Targeted surveillance and potential assassination attempts against senior officials and key staff; 4) Active information leaks and compromised communications channels; 5) Ongoing cyber intrusions aimed at logistics and command systems. Recommended immediate actions (execute now): A) Secure sensitive sites and tighten access control; conduct rapid vetting of recent staff changes; B) Enforce communications security: rotate keys, suspend and isolate compromised accounts, require verified channels for critical orders; C) Authorize SBU to task field teams to contain and detain identified persons of interest—request operational support from GUR/Budanov for arrests/raids; D) MOD: place designated rapid-reaction and protection units on standby to secure infrastructure and provide force support to SBU operations; E) Klymenko/Police: increase checkpoints, protective details, and counter-surveillance in Kyiv; F) GUR: immediately forward location-specific imminent threat intel and IED/sabotage indicators to SBU for tasking. SBU will produce a high-priority POI list and an action plan within 30 minutes. Request Zelenskyy/Yermak approval to commence immediate containment operations with MOD support. GUR — please present your frontline/imminent-threat report now.

GUR update & requests: 1) GUR will deliver detailed annexes/maps/ISR feeds to OPS within 20 minutes and the prioritized SEAD/precision target list within 15 minutes; ready to hand over target packs for immediate strike tasking. 2) MOD/Syrskyi: confirm unit, exact departure time, route and ETA for the mechanized reserve reposition to Bakhmut/Avdiivka now (Syrskyi ordered confirmation within 2 hours). If approved, GUR recommends departure within ~2 hours and ETA ~4–6 hours — state which unit and route so we can adjust ISR coverage. 3) MOD/Oleshchuk: provide AD allocation map, interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery timelines within 45 minutes so GUR can finalize coverage. 4) SBU: confirm legal/ROE vetting and counter‑sabotage prioritization — advise if legal vetting for proposed SEAD/strikes will complete within 30 minutes. 5) GUR requests formal authorization to hand over validated target sets to MOD and to coordinate strike timing; request acknowledgement and any blockers now.

GUR urgent — immediate confirmations required: (1) MOD/Syrskyi: state exact mechanized reserve unit approved, departure time, route, ETA to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, and expected combat readiness on arrival (fuel/ammo). (2) MOD/Oleshchuk: publish AD allocation map and interceptor/ammo quantities with earliest delivery ETAs within 45 minutes. (3) SBU: confirm legal/ROE vetting timeline for proposed SEAD/precision strikes — can clearance be completed within 30 minutes? If any timeline cannot be met, state the specific blocker and the earliest possible ETA. GUR will deliver annexes and prioritized target packs within 15–20 minutes and needs these confirmations to finalize strike tasking and AD coverage.

Валерий Владимирович, прошу краткий доклад по общей оперативной обстановке и ключевым угрозам на фронте.

Господин Президент, уважаемый Сергей Кужугетович. Краткий доклад по ситуации на восточном направлении.

1) Общая обстановка: фронт в целом стабилен, противник ведёт локальные контратаки и пытается восстанавливать свои тыловые сети снабжения; наши подразделения удерживают господствующие рубежи в приоритетных секторах, но отмечается рост темпов истощения материально-технических ресурсов и боеприпасов в отдельных группировках.

2) Ключевые направления и цели: приоритет — обеспечить устойчивость оборонных рубежей и создать условия для ограниченных оперативно-стратегических наступательных действий там, где это даст тактическое и стратегическое преимущество; сохранить контроль над коммуникациями и нарушить линию снабжения противника; минимизировать собственные потери и сохранить боеспособность формирований.

3) Оперативная оценка: боеспособность частей в целом удовлетворительная, но отдельные соединения требуют ротации и пополнения личного состава и запаса боеприпасов; ПВО и РЭБ выполняют важную защитную функцию, однако нуждаются в усилении в зонах повышенной угрозы; разведка даёт достаточный общий обзор, но существует дефицит оперативных данных по ряду тыловых узлов противника.

4) Основные риски: риск перегрузки логистики и исчерпания боеприпасного резерва при продолжении текущих темпов операций; вероятность внезапных контратак противника при локальном превосходстве; усиление материально-технической поддержки противника из-за внешней помощи; погодные и дорожные условия, снижающие мобильность; информационное и дипломатическое давление.

5) Предлагаемые немедленные распоряжения (стратегического/организационного характера):
   - Утвердить режим приоритетного пополнения и ротации для наиболее уязвимых соединений; выделить мобильные резервы для быстрого переброса на критические участки.
   - Сосредоточить усилия на обеспечении устойчивости логистических коридоров: приоритет ремонта мостов, дорог и пополнения горючим и боеприпасами.
   - Усилить систему ПВО и РЭБ в полосах, где фиксируется усиление ударной активности противника; принять меры по защите тыловой инфраструктуры.
   - Интенсифицировать разведку (воздушную и техническую) для уточнения позиций противника и раннего выявления подготовок к контратакам; активизировать разведывательные беспилотные средства там, где это допустимо.
   - Ограничить масштабы наступательных действий до задач, обеспечивающих оперативную выгоду и приемлемый уровень риска; избегать необоснованного расширения фронта без гарантии снабжения и резервов.
   - Координировать коммуникацию с Минобороны и МИД по ключевым информационно-дипломатическим аспектам операций.
   - Подготовить планы на случай ухудшения обстановки: сценарии удержания, организованной отводки и подтверждённых контрмер по логистике и медицинской эвакуации.

Если Президенты и министр одобряют, приказываю штабу и командующим начать немедленную подготовку к реализации этих мер и доложить о конкретных потребностях в резервах, боеприпасах и инженерной технике для утверждения.

Господин Президент, уважаемый Сергей Кужугетович. Краткий оперативный свод по ключевым направлениям и срочные приказы.

1) Авдеевка: обороняемся устойчиво, противник проводит локальные контратаки с целью истощения наших позиций. Наши подразделения держат рубеж, но критически сокращены запасы артиллерийских боеприпасов и горючего в ряде частей. Срочно: приоритетная доставка боеприпасов и горючего, ротация наиболее истощённых батальонов, выделение мобильного резерва для прикрытия населённых пунктов и узлов снабжения.

2) Бахмут: наиболее высокая интенсивность боевых действий и потерь; ряд соединений требует пополнения личным составом и медицинской сортировки. Срочно: ограничить наступательные усилия до целей, дающих тактический выигрыш; усилить противотанковую и артиллерийскую поддержку там, где удержание рубежей критично; организовать ускоренную эвакуацию и пополнение раненных.

3) Херсонское направление: ситуация более подвижная, контроль над переправами и ключевыми дорогами — приоритет. Срочно: обеспечить инженерные работы по восстановлению мостов и дорог, усилить охрану логистических коридоров и ПВО в районах базирования тыловых узлов.

4) Боеспособность и потери: в целом боеспособность формирований удовлетворительная, но отдельные бригады находятся на уровне сниженной боеготовности (требуют ротации и пополнения); темпы потерь остаются проблемой для поддержания баланса боевых сил.

5) Резервы и их расположение: мобильные резервы и материальные запасы сосредоточены в Белгородской и Ростовской областях и на южном направлении (Крым) — предлагаю ускорить переброску и подготовить резервные эшелоны топлива и боеприпасов к ближайшим узлам снабжения.

6) Разведка и ПВО/РЭБ: усилить координатную работу воздушной и технической разведки, увеличить использование БПЛА для раннего обнаружения подготовок к контратакам; усилить ПВО и РЭБ в зонах повышенной угрозы.

7) Немедленные приказы для выполнения штабу и командования: а) приоритетное распределение боеприпасов и топлива по уязвимым соединениям; б) начать ротацию частей с пониженной боеготовностью; в) выделить и поставить в наряд мобильные резервы для критических участков; г) запустить инженерные работы по восстановлению коммуникаций; д) усилить ПВО/РЭБ и разведку в приоритетных секторах; е) ограничить наступательные операции рамками обеспеченности и логистики.
