1) 在60分钟内以书面形式向克里姆林和莫斯科提交可调派至莫斯科的部队/单元清单（按编成与兵种）、人员与关键装备名单、预计出动与到达时间、运输方式与护送需求、后勤/燃油/医疗需求；
2) 明确并报送可持续提供的PVO与空中巡逻力量构成、可维持时限及部署地点；
3) 指派并报送一名联络官（姓名、职务、移动电话）与莫斯科市运作联络点对接；
索比亚宁：请在30分钟内提交最终优先保护目标清单（名称、地址、接收联邦部队的坐标与接收点）、现有损伤/高风险点与拟接收力量的对接人信息。所有收到本指示者请短回确认已收悉并给出最早可完成时间窗。普京知悉。

data.content: Permission granted. GUR — begin your 3‑minute briefing now: focus on imminent frontline threats, air/missile attacks, and recommended immediate actions. SBU, Budanov, MOD/Syrskyi, Oleshchuk, Klitschko, Kyrylenko, Podolyak, Yermak — be ready to brief in order after GUR.

Urgent SBU: convene immediate counterintelligence briefing here now. GUR — present your 3–5 minute report on imminent threats. SBU (me) will follow with internal threats and countermeasures. MOD — be ready to mobilize forces on recommended actions.

SBU report (3–5 min): Immediate internal counterintelligence threats: 1) Hostile infiltration/insider compromise within Kyiv security and at some critical facilities; 2) Planned sabotage of energy, communications, and attempts to degrade air-defence C2; 3) Targeted surveillance and potential assassination attempts against senior officials and key staff; 4) Active information leaks and compromised communications channels; 5) Ongoing cyber intrusions aimed at logistics and command systems. Recommended immediate actions (execute now): A) Secure sensitive sites and tighten access control; conduct rapid vetting of recent staff changes; B) Enforce communications security: rotate keys, suspend and isolate compromised accounts, require verified channels for critical orders; C) Authorize SBU to task field teams to contain and detain identified persons of interest—request operational support from GUR/Budanov for arrests/raids; D) MOD: place designated rapid-reaction and protection units on standby to secure infrastructure and provide force support to SBU operations; E) Klymenko/Police: increase checkpoints, protective details, and counter-surveillance in Kyiv; F) GUR: immediately forward location-specific imminent threat intel and IED/sabotage indicators to SBU for tasking. SBU will produce a high-priority POI list and an action plan within 30 minutes. Request Zelenskyy/Yermak approval to commence immediate containment operations with MOD support. GUR — please present your frontline/imminent-threat report now.

Orders, effective immediately: 1) MOD/Syrskyi & Ministry of Defence — authorize reposition of one mechanized reserve to the most threatened sectors (Bakhmut/Avdiivka) and increase coastal/port force posture. Navy: raise patrol and escort tempo, harden berths, protect grain shipments and port approaches. 2) Air Force/Oleshchuk — concentrate SAM/AD coverage over critical hubs (Odesa, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia), surge CAP sorties and scramble intercepts, disperse and harden logistics/fuel points. Approve limited SEAD/precision strikes on validated missile‑launch and sensor/C2 nodes — GUR to provide target validation. 3) GUR/Budanov — push immediate ISR/missile launch coordinates, EW targets, and the three 1‑page annexes; prioritize C2 nodes for EW/SEAD. 4) SBU/Klymenko — step up counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv critical infrastructure and port facilities. 5) Regional authorities/Kyrylenko & Klitschko — begin evacuations and sheltering for vulnerable port areas; reinforce Kyiv security. 6) Podolyak/Yermak — urgent diplomatic outreach to allies for AD interceptor/munition resupply and prepare public messaging. Logistics: disperse fuel/munitions stocks now. I grant authority to execute these measures; report back status and any requests for further authority every 15 minutes.

Report: Antalya grain‑deal talks collapsed and our southern ports have been attacked. Convene immediate briefings in OPS in 15 minutes: SBU (security/sabotage assessment), MOD/Syrskyi (force posture, Navy representation for port/escort options), GUR/Budanov (damage, ISR, enemy intent), Air Force/Oleshchuk (AD/escort capability), Kyiv/klitschko & regional Kyrylenko (civil protection/evacuations), Podolyak/Yermak (diplomatic/partner notifications). Each team must deliver: 1) concise situation assessment (ports affected, damage, casualties, ships/loads impacted, maritime control); 2) immediate threats and POIs (sabotage/strike risk); 3) recommended actions (naval escorts, port hardening, alternate export corridors, emergency diplomatic asks) with required resources and ETAs; 4) any blockers. If you cannot meet the 15‑minute window, post the blocker and earliest ETA now. Report back in‑thread and be ready to brief to the full council.

Господин Президент, коллеги. Кратко по ситуации: переговоры в Анталии сорваны; после ухода Лаврова южные порты Украины подверглись новой волне блокирующих обстрелов; обстановка в Одессе и на южном фланге резко обострилась. Я прибыл в Крым для координации ответных мер. Предлагаю три конкретных варианта действий с приоритетами и оценкой рисков:

1) Приоритет 1 — сосредоточить усилия на обеспечении контроля над подходами к Черному и Азовскому морю и помешать восстановлению экспортной инфраструктуры противника. Риск: значительная международная политическая реакция и эскалация инцидентов на море; смягчение: выработка ясной юридической аргументации, публичные предупреждения для гражданских судов, строгое ограничение ответных мер по времени и масштабу.

2) Приоритет 2 — провести ограниченные, тщательно подготовленные удары по ключевой логистической и портовой инфраструктуре противника с целью существенного снижения его экспортного потенциала. Риск: гражданские потери и дипломатические последствия, усиление антироссийской риторики; смягчение: обязательная правовая проверка целей, максимальное применение разведданных для минимизации сопутствующего ущерба, согласование информационной линии.

3) Приоритет 3 — активизировать дипломатические и информационные усилия для подрыва внешней поддержки операций по вывозу и параллельно работать над экономическими и транспортными альтернативами для наших поставок. Риск: медленное влияние на оперативную обстановку; смягчение: синхронизация дипломатии с военными действиями и координация с экономическими ведомствами.

Прошу указание: дать разрешение на оперативную проработку плана по варианту 1 и, при одобрении, подготовить детализированную оценку ресурсов и временных рамок по варианту 2. Готов приступить к докладу по деталям разведывательной картины и ожидаемым эффектам.

Acknowledged. The meeting is called to order. General Gerasimov, please present the overall situation first. Minister Shoigu and Spokesman Konashenkov will follow. Mayor Sobyanin, please hold your remarks until invited.

Minister Shoigu: provide immediate, detailed reports covering (1) troop readiness by unit and location, (2) casualties and combat losses, and (3) logistics and supply status (ammunition, fuel, medical, transport). Specify current resource shortfalls, required reinforcements, and estimated timelines to restore capability. Prepare a concise executive summary for President Putin, General Gerasimov, and Spokesman Konashenkov and deliver within 2 hours, highlighting key figures, critical gaps, and recommended urgent actions.
Принято, Ваше Святейшество. Благодарим за молитвенную поддержку. Просим подготовить краткое слово и выступить позже в совещании по приглашению.

Генерал Валерий Владимирович, докладывайте общую оперативную обстановку немедленно. Одновременно прошу представить оперативные сводки по Авдеевке, Бахмуту и Херсону к 12:00: боеспособность частей по подразделениям, потери, дислокация резервов и срочные приказы для их обеспечения, а также первоочередные потребности. Министр Шойгу и спикер Конашенков — приготовьте после доклада детализацию по ресурсам, логистике и информационной линии. Министр Лавров и Песков — синхронизируйте внешнеполитическую и публичную коммуникацию по мере поступления данных. Мэр Собянин — оставайтесь на связи для немедленной поддержки Москвы по вызову.

Господин Конашенков, обеспечьте синхронизацию публичной информационной линии с оценками и распоряжениями Минобороны и Генштаба (Шойгу, Герасимов). Нужна немедленная краткая сводка для брифинга (одна страница): ключевые факты, утверждённые тезисы для СМИ, возможные риски и рекомендованные формулировки. Представить в течение 30 минут. Координируйте окончательные формулировки с Песковым; министр Шойгу и генерал Герасимов — подтвердите соответствие и готовность одобрить линию. Подтвердите получение и ожидаемое время доставки.

Генерал Валерий Владимирович — подтверждаю получение. Немедленно пришлите ФИО и контакт (моб. телефон, резервный номер) назначенного оперативного офицера Штаба для прямой связи с Кремлём и Песковым. Подтвердите точное время вашей презентации сейчас и статус подготовки оперативных сводов по Авдеевке, Бахмуту и Херсону (боеспособность по подразделениям, потери, дислокация резервов, срочные приказы) к 12:00. В течение 1 часа направьте ваши рекомендованные немедленные действия и конкретные запросы на ресурсы (по типам и ориентировочным количествам: ПВО, РЭБ, боеприпасы, инженерная техника, резервные силы). Министр Шойгу — подтвердите наличие и сроки переброски запрошенных ресурсов. Конашенков — подготовьте оперативную одностраничную сводку для брифинга, согласуйте формулировки с Песковым после утверждения свода. Ожидаю срочного ответа.

data.content: Order: Based on GUR's report I approve the following immediate measures. 1) GUR — send the detailed maps, ISR feeds and the three 1‑page annexes now and nominate validated launch/sensor nodes for strikes within 30 minutes. 2) MOD / Oleshchuk — concentrate SAM/AD assets to create layered coverage over critical logistics and energy hubs, provide an AD allocation map and timing within 45 minutes, and increase CAP sorties where available. 3) SBU (Klymenko) — heighten counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv and identified critical nodes immediately. 4) Budanov — prepare limited SEAD/precision strike packages against validated missile launch/sensor nodes; target list to be cleared by GUR and MOD under existing ROE. 5) MOD / me — authorize repositioning of one mechanized reserve to the highest‑risk sector (Bakhmut/Avdiivka); MOD to give proposed unit, route and ETA within 2 hours. 6) Zelenskyy / Yermak / Podolyak — expedite urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions; prepare political/strategic messaging. 7) All — harden and disperse logistics and fuel points now. Report back with status and any blocking issues in 1 hour.

Received and understood. Actions I will take now: 1) Produce and deliver an AD allocation map with layered coverage and timing within 45 minutes. 2) Increase CAP sortie rates where munitions permit and send proposed CAP tasking within 30 minutes. 3) Concentrate SAM/AD assets and begin hardening/dispersal of logistics and fuel points immediately; I will report implementation status. 4) Coordinate with Budanov on SEAD/precision‑strike packages — I require GUR target nominations and their maps/ISR now (as ordered). 5) On repositioning a mechanized reserve: I will coordinate with MOD for the proposed unit, route and ETA and stand ready to provide air support for movement. Constraints/blockers: interceptor and strike‑munition stocks are currently limited (urgent external resupply required), EW suppression assets are in demand, and ISR protection remains critical. I will report back with map, tasking, and any blocking issues within 1 hour.

Acknowledged and decisions: 1) MOD — repositioning one mechanized reserve to Bakhmut/Avdiivka is authorized. MOD to confirm unit, departure time, route and ETA within 2 hours. 2) SEAD/precision strikes — authorized against validated launch/sensor nodes. Budanov to prepare strike packages; GUR and MOD to clear targets under existing ROE. 3) GUR — deliver the three annexes, maps and ISR feeds and nominate prioritized launch/sensor nodes within 30 minutes. 4) MOD / Oleshchuk — provide an AD allocation map and timing within 45 minutes and increase CAP sorties where available; publish interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest delivery timelines. 5) SBU (Klymenko) — heighten counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv and identified critical nodes; activate sheltering plans for likely strike windows. 6) President / Yermak / Podolyak — expedite urgent resupply of AD interceptors and munitions and prepare political/strategic messaging. 7) All — harden and disperse logistics and fuel points now. Report status and any blockers in 1 hour. If anyone requires specific additional information, state exactly what and from whom now.

Acknowledged, Mr President. Air Force actions and timetable: 1) Produce AD allocation map with layered coverage for Odesa, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia within 45 minutes. 2) Provide CAP sortie tasking and proposed surge within 30 minutes (subject to munitions availability). 3) Begin immediate dispersal and hardening of logistics and fuel points and report implementation. 4) Coordinate with GUR/Budanov for validated target nominations, ISR feeds and the three annexes — request delivery now. 5) Coordinate with MOD/Syrskyi on the proposed mechanized reserve unit, route and ETA; Air Force stands ready to provide movement air support. Constraints/blockers: interceptor and strike‑munition stocks are limited; EW suppression assets and ISR protection remain critical. I will report status and any requests every 15 minutes.

Immediate coordination: Air Force will begin drafting the AD allocation map and CAP tasking now and will deliver final AD allocation map and proposed CAP tasking within 45 minutes. Requests/actions required immediately: 1) MOD — send current SAM/AD asset locations and disposition, interceptor counts by battery, and earliest resupply ETAs; confirm which SAM/AD systems can be reallocated to provide layered coverage for Odesa, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia. 2) GUR/Budanov — deliver the annexes/maps, validated SEAD/precision target list, and live ISR feeds to Air Force OPS now (request delivery within 15 minutes) and mark priority C2/SEAD and launch/sensor nodes for AD/SEAD planning. 3) Syrskyi/MOD — confirm exact mechanized reserve unit approved, route, departure window and ETA so Air Force can plan movement air support and protective AD coverage. Note constraints: interceptor and strike‑munition shortages, high demand for EW/ISR protection — state any blockers or shortfalls now. I will produce draft AD allocation and CAP tasking and circulate for MOD/GUR review within 45 minutes.

Mr President — I confirm authorization to reposition one mechanized reserve to the Bakhmut/Avdiivka sector. Ministry of Defence (ukrainian_mod): confirm the exact assigned unit, planned departure time, route, ETA, and expected combat readiness on arrival (fuel/ammo levels and sustain requirements) within 2 hours as previously ordered. GUR/Budanov: task ISR to monitor the route and provide en‑route threat updates and recommended escorts. Air Force/Oleshchuk: prepare air cover and AD support for the movement and state earliest CAP/air‑support availability. SBU/Klymenko: coordinate route security and counter‑sabotage measures. State any blockers or constraints immediately.

Attention all: Air Force OPS will produce the AD allocation map with layered coverage and the proposed CAP tasking within 45 minutes. Immediate actions required now: 1) GUR/Budanov — deliver annexes, maps, validated SEAD/precision target list and live ISR feeds (digital push + one liaison to Air Force OPS) within 15 minutes. 2) MOD/Syrskyi/ukrainian_mod — send current SAM/AD locations and dispositions, interceptor counts by battery, earliest resupply ETAs, and confirm which systems can be reallocated; provide one liaison to OPS immediately. 3) SBU/Klymenko — secure AD command nodes, movement routes and confirm counter‑sabotage coverage for planned movements. 4) Klitschko — confirm Kyiv protection measures and liaison for civil coordination. State any blockers or shortfalls now. Air Force OPS will circulate draft AD allocation and CAP tasking for MOD/GUR review as soon as ready.

Orders/confirmations: 1) Authorization — I formally authorize GUR/Budanov to hand over validated SEAD/precision strike target packs to MOD for immediate tasking. 2) Conditions — SBU/legal (Klymenko): complete ROE/legal vetting of the provided target sets within 30 minutes; if you cannot, state the specific blocker and earliest ETA now. 3) MOD (ukrainian_mod): confirm receipt of the target packs when delivered and confirm strike execution authority/constraints; and CONFIRM the exact mechanized reserve unit assigned to reposition to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, planned departure window, route and ETA within the previously ordered 2‑hour window — if you can state unit and route now, do so so GUR can align ISR. 4) Air Force (Oleshchuk): provide AD allocation map with layered coverage and publish interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest resupply ETAs within 45 minutes; state CAP surge (sortie numbers/rate) now if available and availability to provide air cover for the movement. 5) GUR: deliver the three annexes, prioritized validated target list and live ISR feeds to OPS within 15–20 minutes and mark highest‑priority C2/SEAD/launch/sensor nodes for immediate tasking. 6) All: if any timeline cannot be met, state the specific blocker and the earliest possible ETA now. Acknowledge this thread on receipt and report any blockers immediately.

Air Force OPS orders (execute now): 1) Send ONE liaison physically to Air Force OPS (Kyiv ops center) immediately and perform a secure digital push of all annexes/maps/ISR feeds and SAM/AD data. 2) GUR/Budanov — deliver validated SEAD/precision target list and live ISR feed link within 15 minutes. 3) MOD/ukrainian_mod/Syrskyi — deliver current SAM/AD locations and dispositions, interceptor counts by battery, which systems can be reallocated, and earliest resupply ETAs within 20 minutes. 4) SBU/Klymenko — confirm route security, AD command‑node protection and counter‑sabotage coverage for planned movements now. Reply in this thread with the liaison’s name and ETA to OPS within 10 minutes and state any blockers.

Immediate confirmations required — reply in this thread now with exact ETAs/blockers: 1) MOD (ukrainian_mod): state the exact mechanized reserve unit assigned to reposition to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, planned departure window, route, ETA, and expected combat readiness on arrival (fuel/ammo/sustain). 2) Air Force (oleshchuk): confirm delivery of the AD allocation map and CAP tasking within 45 minutes, publish interceptor/ammo quantities and earliest resupply ETAs, and state CAP surge (sortie numbers/rate) and availability to provide air cover for the movement. 3) GUR (gur/budanov): confirm delivery ETA for the three annexes, prioritized validated SEAD/launch/sensor/C2 target list and live ISR feeds (expected within 15–20 minutes) and confirm target validation status. 4) SBU (klymenko): confirm ability to complete ROE/legal vetting of provided target sets within 30 minutes and provide the high‑priority POI list within 30 minutes. If any timeline cannot be met, state the specific blocker and the earliest possible ETA. Acknowledge receipt.

Confirmed: I can access the eShare package at https://eshare.un.int/black-sea-grain/pack-15-30 and the final participant list (me, the Emergency Relief Coordinator, the USG for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, the Legal Adviser, and you) is correct. Please upload the pending secure mobile/Signal numbers to eShare once consent is received (option a). If any of those numbers are urgently required before consent, send them to me now as a separate encrypted message. I have no immediate edits to the draft resolution; if colleagues submit tracked‑change edits, please upload the .docx to eShare and flag them for my attention. Notify me when the pending items are uploaded. I will join from New York at 15:30 GMT.

Permission granted. Begin the briefing now. Present, in order: (1) current frontline picture and any critical shifts or breakthroughs; (2) air/missile threats expected in the next 24 hours — likely vectors, timing, and confidence levels; (3) recommended immediate actions (air-defence posture, urgent force movements, civilian protection/evacuations, critical infrastructure protection); (4) urgent resource requests with timelines (ammo, interceptors, logistics, medical). Prioritize items by immediacy and required decision level (Presidential/Cabinet/MOD). I expect concise, actionable recommendations — proceed.

All — following GUR's briefing, we need immediate decisions and ETAs. 1) MOD/Cabinet: approve repositioning one mechanized reserve to the Bakhmut/Avdiivka sector to plug attrition gaps. MOD to confirm unit, departure time, and ETA. 2) President/General Staff: authorize limited SEAD/precision strikes on validated missile‑launch / sensor nodes to blunt incoming strike waves. GUR to provide prioritized target list; SBU to confirm legal/ROE vetting. 3) Air defence: concentrate SAM/AD coverage on logistics, fuel, energy, and key transport hubs; increase CAP where available. MOD/AD to publish required interceptors/ammo quantities and earliest delivery timelines. 4) Internal security/civil protection: SBU and Kyiv city — step up counter‑sabotage, harden critical nodes, and activate sheltering plans for likely strike windows. 5) GUR: deliver the promised annexes, maps, and ISR feeds to the ops center within 30 minutes. Reply in this thread with your decisions, any objections, and clear ETAs. If additional information is required, state specifically what and from whom.

MOD/Syrskyi/Oleshchuk — confirm immediately: (A) Which mechanized reserve unit is approved to reposition to the Bakhmut/Avdiivka sector; (B) exact departure time and planned route; (C) ETA at the front and expected combat readiness on arrival (fuel, ammo levels); (D) any force protection/logistics constraints that could delay movement. Air defence (Oleshchuk/MOD) — publish required interceptor and ammunition quantities and earliest delivery timelines (source/unit and ETA). Provide clear answers in this thread within 15 minutes; if you cannot meet that deadline, state the blocker and the earliest possible ETA.

Confirmed decisions and immediate orders (execute now; reply with confirmations/ETAs or blockers):

1) Mechanized reserve — APPROVED. MOD/Syrskyi: confirm unit designation, exact departure window, route, ETA to Bakhmut/Avdiivka, and force‑protection/logistics plan within 2 hours (provide unit ID and earliest possible departure within 30–60 min if available). Provide availability of military escorts and engineering units for hardened logistics/fuel moves now.

2) GUR deliverables — GUR: deliver three 1‑page annexes, detailed frontline maps, live ISR feeds and prioritized validated SEAD/launch/sensor/C2 list (coords, timestamps, confidence) within 15–20 minutes.

3) Legal/ROE & strike vetting — SBU/Klymenko: complete legal/ROE vetting of GUR target list within 30 minutes or state blockers now; begin counter‑sabotage sweeps and provide high‑priority POI and concrete action plan to Kyiv ops in 30 minutes; initial status/report in 1 hour.

4) Air‑defence resourcing — Oleshchuk/MOD: publish AD allocation map, interceptor and magazine counts, and earliest delivery ETAs within 45 minutes (if you cannot meet 45 min, state blocker and earliest ETA now). State exact interceptor/munition shortfalls (quantities) so diplomatic tasking can proceed.

5) SEAD/strike packages — Budanov: prepare ready SEAD/precision strike packages coordinated with MOD and GUR within 2 hours; advise required assets/timing and any limits to execution.

6) Kyiv civil measures — Klitschko: confirm shelter activation status, published shelter locations/capacities, POI/action plan in 30 minutes and full status/blockers in 1 hour; request military support if needed for protection/movements.

7) Diplomacy/logistics — Podolyak/Yermak: begin urgent outreach to partners for interceptors, munitions, mobile AD and emergency engineering once shortfall list available; prepare public/diplomatic drafts per UkGov timeline (45 min).

Reporting cadence: report blockers immediately and execution status every 15 minutes in this thread. If any addressee cannot meet the deadline, state the precise blocker and earliest achievable ETA now.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We will finalise UK team names and timelines now. I confirm Brigadier Claire Foster as UK team lead and point of contact. UK nominations are: Team Lead — Brigadier Claire Foster; Air‑defence/SHORAD training lead — Lt Col James Mercer; Long‑range fires training lead — Lt Col Sarah Patel; C‑UAS lead — Maj Tom Harding; Logistics/Sustainment lead — Lt Col Robert Hayes; ISR/EW lead — Sqn Ldr David Price; Liaison officers — Capt Anna Lewis and Capt Mark Thompson; Planning cell lead — Maj Emily Carter. This UK embedding package will comprise the 6 trainer‑instructors, 3 logisticians/sustainment specialists, 2 ISR/EW specialists and 2 liaison officers previously described, organised under the above leads.

Timelines to meet your target: initial high‑priority 0–30 day shipments and trainer‑deployment list within 48 hours; consolidated 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan within 72 hours. We will circulate a draft Terms of Reference, draft timetable and secure contact details for Brigadier Foster and the UK team in the secure channel within 6 hours to support your sign‑off.

Please confirm acceptance of these UK names and timelines and, when available, send your nominated Ukrainian POC and the prioritized spreadsheet so the joint team can begin drafting the 0–30/30–60/60–90 plan immediately.

General Sir Tony — I confirm acceptance of the UK team, nominees and proposed timelines. I nominate Colonel Andriy Kovalenko as the Ukrainian senior planning officer and point of contact; I will transmit his secure contact details and the prioritized spreadsheet with suggested quantities and any embedding constraints within 12 hours. We accept the proposed liaison architecture and embedding caveats as noted. Please proceed to circulate the draft Terms of Reference and timetable in the secure channel so the joint team can begin drafting the 0–30/30–60/60–90 plan on receipt of our spreadsheet.

Brigadier Foster — I am transmitting Colonel Andriy Kovalenko's secure contact details and the prioritized spreadsheet to you and the UK team now via the agreed secure channel. Colonel Kovalenko is the Ukrainian senior planning officer and POC. The secure contact and spreadsheet have been uploaded to the secure channel; please confirm receipt and advise when the joint team can begin drafting the 0–30/30–60/60–90 plan.

General Zaluzhnyi — we have assembled the UK team and are circulating the draft Terms of Reference, draft timetable and UK secure contact details in the agreed secure channel now.

Draft TOR (summary): Purpose — produce a consolidated 0/30/60/90‑day delivery & integration plan in support of Ukrainian operational priorities. Key tasks — consolidate your prioritized spreadsheet; produce a prioritized 0–30 shipments & trainer‑deployment list (48 hours); produce full 30/60/90 delivery, training and sustainment plan (72 hours). Responsibilities — UK planning cell to coordinate drafting; UK leads to populate capability annexes (AD/SHORAD, C‑UAS, long‑range fires, training, logistics, ISR/EW). Coordination — embedded brigade liaisons + UK–Ukrainian joint coordination cell at operational HQ; security approvals required for embedding. Reporting — daily planning cell sync (first 72 hours), immediate escalation of critical shortfalls.

Draft timetable (summary): Hour 0 — secure receipt of Ukrainian spreadsheet and Colonel Kovalenko contact; Hours 0–24 — planning cell consolidation and annex drafting; By 48 hrs — deliver initial high‑priority 0–30 shipments & trainer list; By 72 hrs — deliver consolidated 30/60/90 plan and recommended delivery/training timelines.

UK secure contacts (uploaded to secure channel): Brigadier Claire Foster (Team Lead) — foster.sec; Planning cell lead Maj Emily Carter — carter.sec; AD/SHORAD lead Lt Col James Mercer — mercer.sec; Long‑range fires lead Lt Col Sarah Patel — patel.sec; C‑UAS lead Maj Tom Harding — harding.sec; Logistics lead Lt Col Robert Hayes — hayes.sec; ISR/EW lead Sqn Ldr David Price — price.sec; Liaison officers Capt Anna Lewis — lewis.sec and Capt Mark Thompson — thompson.sec.

Action requested: please confirm receipt in the secure channel and confirm Colonel Andriy Kovalenko’s secure contact so the joint team can begin drafting immediately on receipt of your spreadsheet.

The UK planning cell will begin drafting immediately. We will hold an initial planning‑cell sync within 2 hours, consolidate annex inputs over the next 24 hours, deliver the prioritized 0–30 shipments and trainer‑deployment list within 48 hours, and deliver the consolidated 30/60/90 plan within 72 hours. Brigadier Foster will post any clarification questions to the secure channel; please advise of any immediate security caveats or restrictions we should note for embedding.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. I welcome Colonel Kovalenko’s nomination and note Brigadier Foster’s confirmation of receipt. The UK planning cell will begin drafting immediately and will post any clarification questions to the secure channel. I would like to meet in person to agree the liaison architecture and the security approvals required for embedding UK trainers and liaisons — are you available for a brief meeting now or later today? Please also flag any immediate operational caveats we should know before embedding.

General Sir Tony / Brigadier Foster — received, thank you. Colonel Kovalenko will join the initial planning‑cell sync and is standing by in the secure channel. Immediate security caveats for embedding: (1) all UK personnel must undergo Ukrainian security vetting and formal approval before deployment; (2) embedding will be limited to brigade HQs and operational‑HQ rear areas unless an explicit, approved exception is agreed; (3) UK teams will not operate forward of approved lines or accompany combat patrols without prior agreement and agreed force‑protection measures; (4) movement routes, force‑protection and logistic corridors for UK personnel and equipment must be coordinated through Ukrainian security and logistics channels; and (5) sensitive reporting/material must use the agreed secure handling procedures. Please propose the planning‑cell sync time and any immediate clarification questions — Colonel Kovalenko will be online to support the UK team.

General Sir Tony — I can meet in person now or later today. I propose 16:00 UK time in the secure MOD conference room; if you prefer to meet immediately I am ready. Colonel Kovalenko will join the initial planning‑cell sync and can attend the in‑person meeting if Ukrainian security approvals permit. Please confirm whether you want to meet now or at 16:00 and confirm the planning‑cell sync time (I propose start in one hour if that suits Brigadier Foster).

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. I will meet at 16:00 UK time in the secure MOD conference room. Brigadier Foster will chair the initial planning‑cell sync, which we will start in one hour to begin consolidation; Colonel Kovalenko is invited to join. If you are ready now, I suggest we start with: (1) liaison architecture (brigade‑level liaisons + joint coordination cell), (2) security‑vetting timelines and embedding approvals for UK personnel, and (3) any immediate constraints on unit priorities or movement/force‑protection corridors. Permission granted. GUR — begin your 3‑minute briefing now: focus on imminent frontline threats, air/missile attacks, and recommended immediate actions. SBU, Budanov, MOD/Syrskyi, Oleshchuk, Klitschko, Kyrylenko, Podolyak, Yermak — be ready to brief in order after GUR.

Orders, effective immediately: 1) MOD/Syrskyi & Ministry of Defence — authorize reposition of one mechanized reserve to the most threatened sectors (Bakhmut/Avdiivka) and increase coastal/port force posture. Navy: raise patrol and escort tempo, harden berths, protect grain shipments and port approaches. 2) Air Force/Oleshchuk — concentrate SAM/AD coverage over critical hubs (Odesa, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia), surge CAP sorties and scramble intercepts, disperse and harden logistics/fuel points. Approve limited SEAD/precision strikes on validated missile‑launch and sensor/C2 nodes — GUR to provide target validation. 3) GUR/Budanov — push immediate ISR/missile launch coordinates, EW targets, and the three 1‑page annexes; prioritize C2 nodes for EW/SEAD. 4) SBU/Klymenko — step up counter‑sabotage and protection of Kyiv critical infrastructure and port facilities. 5) Regional authorities/Kyrylenko & Klitschko — begin evacuations and sheltering for vulnerable port areas; reinforce Kyiv security. 6) Podolyak/Yermak — urgent diplomatic outreach to allies for AD interceptor/munition resupply and prepare public messaging. Logistics: disperse fuel/munitions stocks now. I grant authority to execute these measures; report back status and any requests for further authority every 15 minutes.

DECISIONS & ORDERS — Immediate civil‑protection, martial‑law adjustments, reconstruction priorities, and international requests (implement now; reply with confirmations/ETAs):

1) Martial‑law / movement restrictions (effective immediately):
- Activate heightened martial‑law measures targeted to Kyiv and high‑risk oblasts (Donetsk/Kharkiv/Zaporizhzhia/Odesa/Mykolaiv). Implement a protective curfew during predicted strike windows: movement restricted 23:00–05:00 local (exceptions: emergency services, escorted evacuations, essential logistics with passes). SBU/Klitschko: publish exact local curfew times/areas and rules of exception within 1 hour.

2) Sheltering & prioritized evacuations (activate now):
- Activate national shelter network; Kyiv: open designated shelters, publish locations, capacities, and recommended arrival times within 2 hours. Prioritize hospitals, elderly care homes, dialysis/oncology patients, and children. Klitschko/SBU: commence sheltering and phased evacuations for identified high‑risk districts and port/industrial zones; deliver evacuation timelines and transport plans (who goes where, by when) within 2 hours.

3) Targeted protective measures for critical infrastructure (implement now):
- Immediate hardening/dispersal orders for power substations, water treatment, fuel/logistics hubs, hospitals, and AD C2 nodes. SBU/Klitschko/MOD engineering units: execute physical protection, access control, and redundant power (generators) staging now; submit status and blockers within 2 hours.

4) Curated evacuations for ports & frontline‑adjacent civilian populations:
- Begin phased non‑combatant evacuation of vulnerable port personnel and high‑risk frontline towns on next safe windows (next 6–24 hrs). Regional governors coordinate transit hubs and shelters; Kyrylenko/Klitschko: provide list of prioritized localities and ETAs for movement start within 3 hours.

5) Reconstruction priorities (72‑hour & 30‑day):
- 72‑hour: emergency power to hospitals and water plants (mobile generators + rapid repair teams), restore key hospital access routes, triage capability, emergency potable water delivery, temporary sheltering for displaced. Dispatch emergency engineering & medical rapid‑response teams now. Report resource shortfalls within 3 hours.
- 30‑day: restore primary transmission substations, repair major water treatment infrastructure, reestablish hospital full functionality (power/water/sterilization), and clear/repair primary transport arteries/bridges for logistics — prepare prioritized 30‑day procurement/engineering plan within 48 hours.

6) International assistance — prioritized request tiers (Podolyak/Yermak lead outreach now):
- Tier 1 (Immediate — highest urgency): AD interceptors and munitions; mobile AD batteries/launchers; emergency medical teams + trauma supplies; mobile power/generator convoys; engineering brigades for rapid repair; emergency funding for local authorities; legal/diplomatic backing for attribution and sanctions. (Podolyak/Yermak: begin urgent asks now; specify quantities once MOD/AD list shortfalls.)
- Tier 2 (Next 7–30 days): sustained munitions, more AD systems, heavy engineering equipment, shelter kits, long‑term hospital field support, reconstruction grants/loans.

7) Air‑defense & public safety linkage (MOD/Oleshchuk/GUR):
- MOD/Oleshchuk: publish exact interceptor/ammo shortfalls and earliest delivery windows within 30 minutes (supplier/source & ETAs). GUR: continue to supply predicted salvo windows to schedule shelter/curfew windows precisely. Podolyak/Yermak: attach this shortfall list to diplomatic requests immediately when available.

8) Legal/ROE & SEAD timeline (SBU/MOD/GUR):
- SBU/legal: complete vetting of GUR SEAD/precision target package within 30 minutes or state blockers now. MOD/GUR: hold SEAD execution pending cleared legal vet and Presidential/General Staff signoff. Report status in‑thread.

9) Public & diplomatic messaging (Podolyak/Yermak):
- Prepare two short drafts now: (A) public safety message: explain protective measures, shelter locations, curfew rules, and ask public to follow instructions; (B) diplomatic message to partners: request AD interceptors/medical/engineers, present verified facts and attribution summary (from GUR) and a clear list of urgent needs. Deliver drafts within 45 minutes.

10) Reporting & confirmations (all addressees):
- Reply in‑thread with confirmations, objections, and ETAs per item above. If capability shortfalls exist (interceptors, munitions, engineering lifts, shelter capacity, fuel), list exact quantities and earliest delivery windows so urgent international requests can be finalized.

If no substantive objections within the stated windows, commence implementation now under authorized decision levels. Wake me on any reply and report execution status every 15 minutes.

Report: Antalya grain‑deal talks collapsed and our southern ports have been attacked. Convene immediate briefings in OPS in 15 minutes: SBU (security/sabotage assessment), MOD/Syrskyi (force posture, Navy representation for port/escort options), GUR/Budanov (damage, ISR, enemy intent), Air Force/Oleshchuk (AD/escort capability), Kyiv/klitschko & regional Kyrylenko (civil protection/evacuations), Podolyak/Yermak (diplomatic/partner notifications). Each team must deliver: 1) concise situation assessment (ports affected, damage, casualties, ships/loads impacted, maritime control); 2) immediate threats and POIs (sabotage/strike risk); 3) recommended actions (naval escorts, port hardening, alternate export corridors, emergency diplomatic asks) with required resources and ETAs; 4) any blockers. If you cannot meet the 15‑minute window, post the blocker and earliest ETA now. Report back in‑thread and be ready to brief to the full council.

Mr. President — received your orders and GUR’s briefing. Immediate status (concise):

1) Forces & strikes
- Mechanized reserve reposition: APPROVED and ordered to MOD/Syrskyi; MOD instructed to name the unit, publish departure time, exact route and ETA within 30 minutes. GUR will monitor route ISR. 
- SEAD/precision strikes: CONDITIONALLY APPROVED. GUR is delivering validated target packs; SBU/legal asked to complete ROE vet within 30 minutes. Execution held pending SBU legal clearance and your Presidential/General Staff signoff (please confirm authority to execute once vet is green).

2) Air defence & logistics
- AD posture: MOD/Oleshchuk ordered to concentrate SAM/AD over logistics, energy and key hubs; AD asked to publish exact interceptor/ammo shortfalls and earliest delivery ETAs within 30 minutes. GUR tasked to provide AD coverage‑gap map and redeployment plan within 20 minutes. Podolyak/Yermak have been instructed to attach shortfall list to Tier‑1 diplomatic asks as soon as MOD provides it.

3) Civil protection / martial law
- Heightened martial‑law measures and protective curfews activated for Kyiv and high‑risk oblasts (protective curfew 23:00–05:00 local in predicted strike windows). SBU/Klitschko/Kyiv ops ordered to publish local curfew areas, shelter locations/capacities and phased evacuation timelines within 1–3 hours. Emergency generators, engineering and medical rapid‑response teams dispatched for 72‑hour priorities; 30‑day plan tasked to regionals within 48 hours.

4) International outreach & messaging
- Podolyak/Yermak instructed to send Tier‑1 diplomatic requests to partners (US/UK/DE/PL/CA/EU/NATO) for interceptors, mobile AD, medical teams, generators, engineers and emergency funding — send executed now; partners asked to reply with quantities, dispatch dates and ETAs. Public/diplomatic draft messages tasked and due within 45 minutes.

5) Reporting cadence & requests for you
- All addressees ordered to reply in‑thread with confirmations, ETAs and capability shortfalls; status updates requested every 15 minutes. GUR/SBU/MOD/Oleshchuk/Syrskyi/Klitschko are collating deliverables now.

Request for Presidential action/clarification:
- Please confirm you authorize SEAD/precision strikes to proceed immediately upon SBU legal vet and General Staff confirmation (we currently hold execution pending your signoff).
- Any changes to curfew timing, evacuation priority lists, or public messaging tone/phrasing? If you approve, we will publish drafts and circulate public statement for signature.

We will wake you on any partner replies and report execution/status every 15 minutes. Awaiting your signoff or additional instructions.
